title: A1 adaptation falsification: asymmetry, confidence and carryover tests
hypothesis: If the A1 adapter PPP lift is real coverage response, wrong-way teams should do worse than no-signal teams, the gap should widen with scheme-vote confidence, and adapting in Game N should carry over to Game N+1.
design: Playoff possessions only; game-team cells bucketed adapter/neutral/no_signal/wrong_way; early-to-late third PPP deltas; 430 consecutive (N, N+1) series pairs; one-sided Welch and Mann-Whitney tests.
primary_result: T1 dPPP: adapter +0.0667 (n=205), neutral +0.0248 (n=50), no_signal +0.1260 (n=57), wrong_way +0.0111 (n=274). T2: adapter minus no-signal -0.0361 (1 vote), -0.1170 (2 votes). T3 next-game PPP Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842; MW p=0.863; counter-carry Welch t=-2.163, p=0.985.
failure_evidence: no_signal bucket (+0.1260) beats adapters (+0.0667); gap does not widen with confidence; carryover p=0.84; follow-up showed buckets selected on extreme early-third PPP (regression to mean).
notes: Scheme labels are only assigned when early-third PT PPP is >=10% hot/cold, which mechanically builds in mean reversion; this selection was knowable from the labeling rule before outcomes.

title: A1 within-scheme re-test controlling early-third PPP selection
hypothesis: Within the same inferred scheme (and within early-PPP quintiles), adapters improve PPP more than wrong-way teams, and this carries to the next game.
design: Same playoff cells as A1; adapter vs wrong-way within DROP/HELP/SWITCH, early-PPP quintile matching, and within-scheme Game N to N+1 carryover; Welch and MW tests.
failure_evidence: Quintile-matched gaps near zero in 4 of 5 quintiles; carryover null in all schemes; only DROP within-scheme gap significant without multiplicity correction.
notes: The 'pooled across quintiles' gap +0.0556 equals the unmatched pooled gap, so it is not a matched estimate; flagged.

title: Within-game did_adapt toward SHOULD counters improves PPP
hypothesis: Offenses that shift toward the counter play types for the inferred opponent scheme gain PPP later in the game.
design: 586 playoff game-team rows split into thirds; scheme inferred from early-third PT PPP vs season baseline; did_adapt if counter-PT share rises; compare early-to-late PPP delta.
primary_result: 531 rows with inferred scheme; 249 adapted (46.9%); adapters +0.0701 (n=239) vs non-adapters +0.0121 (n=269), advantage +0.0580 PPP; DROP +0.1001, SWITCH -0.0436, HELP +0.0450.
failure_evidence: A1 falsification: no_signal cells (+0.1260) outperform adapters; selection on extreme early-third PPP causes mean reversion.
notes: Doc calls this 'direct empirical support for the SHOULD logic'; later files in the same folder undercut it.

title: DID-ADAPT case study NYK vs PHI 2025-26 series
hypothesis: Within-game and within-series adaptation toward engine counters coincides with better PPP in one series.
design: 4 games x 2 teams = 8 team-game rows with three-thirds A1 method; series-level SHOULD vs DID cosine (A2).
primary_result: Adapters 4/8 rows; mean dPPP adapters +0.0327 vs non-adapters -0.2987. A2 could not be computed: no SHOULD vector in correction_log.json.
failure_evidence: n=8 team-game rows; series SHOULD vector missing.
notes: Same selection issue as APPA-003 applies.

title: Defensive scheme change within game and across games (inferred labels)
hypothesis: Playoff defenses change scheme within games and between games, especially after the opponent ran a play type heavily.
design: A1 vote-rule scheme inference from opponent PT PPP; 523 comparable within-game cells; 440 consecutive game pairs; heavy-PT conditioning (>=5pp).
primary_result: Within-game change 319/523 (61.0%); cross-game change 298/440 (67.7%); 103/104 units (99.0%) and 52/52 series show a change; transition matrices near-uniform.
failure_evidence: Doc caveat: inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; near-uniform transition matrices consistent with label noise.
notes: Reverse-inferred labels from PPP outcomes; late-third votes use min_n_per_pt=2.

title: Absence validation V1: real absence restructures offense beyond noise
hypothesis: Real present-vs-absent structural displacement D_real exceeds a size-matched subsampling null.
design: Pre-registered; 23 player-seasons, 18 franchises, ON_COURT-verified absences, 2022-25; balanced size-m null (Amendment A1); franchise-clustered permutation and bootstrap.
primary_result: Gate G2 21/23 (91%) above null median; V1(a) 16/23 above own-null p95, binomial p=2.67e-16; V1(b) mean(D_real - median_null)=+0.142, CI [+0.103, +0.187].
failure_evidence: CI excludes 0; binomial p=2.67e-16.
notes: One pre-run amendment (balanced null) because draft null was infeasible when absent>present.

title: Absence validation V2: leave-one-out load predicts real displacement
hypothesis: Fragility leave-one-out load L_pred rank-correlates with real displacement D_real (raw and size-partial).
design: Same pre-registered 23 player-seasons; Spearman with franchise permutation (5000) and cluster bootstrap (2000); post-hoc diagnostics.
primary_result: Gate G3 Spearman +0.099. V2a Spearman +0.288, p=0.077, CI [-0.244, +0.667] FAIL; V2b partial +0.253, p=0.115, CI [-0.262, +0.615] FAIL. Diagnostics: H_code ruled out (rho=0.933); dropping 2 absorption cases rho=+0.444 (n=21).
failure_evidence: 18 franchises below ~20-franchise floor; CI width ~0.9; gate already warned weak (+0.099).
notes: Prereg itself said <20 franchises means underpowered, and the user skipped the full-pool sweep that could have added franchises. Diagnostics also point to a substantive absorption/cascade failure mode.

title: Audit of overnight LLM adaptation-analysis batch ('9/10 adaptation predicts winning')
hypothesis: The agent batch's findings (defensive adjustments, point costs, adaptation predicts series winners 9/10) are valid.
design: Methodology audit of 104 game reports, 10 series, 2073 tool calls; code and graph verification.
primary_result: 706 findings with n<5; list_h2h_games called 0 times; series winners LLM-inferred; MIA-BOS G7 score invented (BOS 100 vs graph 84); what_came_next skips a possession; point costs are LLM arithmetic.
failure_evidence: Series winners never looked up (0/2073 calls); master '9/10' rule built from LLM inference on inference; low-n claims (e.g. 0.0 PPP on n=3).
notes: Half-level PPP splits verified as real; causal and winning claims not validated.

title: Series adaptation experiment: static vs rolling vs adversarial-agent predictors
hypothesis: Adversarial LLM agents predict next-game play-type mix better than static and rolling baselines.
design: 12 playoff series, 4-6 game transitions each (68 transitions); composite accuracy, L1 PT distance, direction/magnitude hit rates, agent hypothesis precision.
primary_result: Rolling beats or ties static in all 12 (e.g. bos_mia 0.835 vs 0.748; den_okc tie agents=rolling 0.859). Agents below rolling in 11/12. Agent Dir%/Mag% 0.0 and L1 scheme 0.000 in every series. Hypothesis precision 0/0 in 9 series, 0/1 (den_min_2324, ind_nyk_2425), 0/2 (lal_hou_2526).
failure_evidence: Agent Dir%/Mag% 0.0 in all 12 series and empty Agent predictions sections in most transitions; the few listed hypotheses (e.g. lal_hou 0/2) never scored as hits.
notes: Updated after reading the remaining 9 series files. Agent arm still looks broken rather than tested; rolling vs static is a real comparison.

title: Adversarial best-response v1: equilibrium strategy vs actual
hypothesis: The system's offensive strategy survives optimal defensive adjustment and beats what teams ran.
design: 240 matchups, 23,922 holdout possessions; iterative best-response to approximate Nash equilibrium, model-scored PPP.
primary_result: Eq vs actual +1.16 pts/100; beats actual 127/240 (53%); vs baseline eq +8.52 pts/100; converged 159/240.
failure_evidence: Doc verdict 'MARGINAL'; equilibrium PPP is model-implied not observed.
notes: Model-scored counterfactual compared to realized PPP.

title: Matchup-aware A3 vs team kernel A2 at equilibrium
hypothesis: Player-vs-defender matchup modeling (A3) improves equilibrium PPP over team-level A2.
design: Same 240 matchups; V2 coarse play types; V3 adds spatial sub-types; V3_SHUFFLED re-run (what was shuffled is not documented).
failure_evidence: Sign flips from +1.34 (V2) to -6.78 (V3) when spatial sub-types were added.
notes: V2 concluded 'MATCHUP MODEL HELPS'; V3 'UNDERPERFORMS'. Shuffled version gives similar numbers.

title: A4 five-player matchup model vs three-player A3
hypothesis: Modeling 5 players per team improves equilibrium PPP over 3.
design: 240 matchups adversarial equilibrium comparison.
failure_evidence: A4-A3 -0.46 pts/100, no test reported.

title: A4 defender-archetype shrinkage layer vs A3
hypothesis: Pooling defenders by archetype improves matchup intelligence.
design: 240 matchups adversarial equilibrium comparison.
failure_evidence: +0.03 pts/100 difference.
notes: File header still says v4.

title: A4 sequence-context modifiers vs A3
hypothesis: Previous-outcome and repetition modifiers lift equilibrium PPP and diversify mixes.
design: 240 matchups; same equilibrium framework.
primary_result: A4 +2.06 vs A3 +2.06; -0.00 pts/100; A4 beats A3 14/240; sample equilibrium mixes identical to A3.
failure_evidence: Identical mixes and exactly 0.0000 deltas suggest the modifiers had no effect (possibly inert in code), not a tested null.

title: A3 equilibrium vs actual significance test
hypothesis: Matchup-aware equilibrium beats actual team behavior significantly across matchups.
design: Per-matchup A3 minus actual across 240 matchups; t-test.
primary_result: A3 beats actual 138/240 (57.5%); weighted mean +2.06 pts/100; median +2.22; SD 14.26; t=2.24; p=0.0644.
failure_evidence: Doc reports p=0.064 not significant.
notes: t=2.24 with n=240 should give p about 0.026 two-sided, so the stated p and t disagree. A3 PPP is nearly constant per offense, e.g. OKC 1.356 against every opponent.

title: Per-team calibration: model 'signal' (bias) vs actual PPP, V1-V6
hypothesis: A3 predicted PPP exceeds actual (treated as validated optimization signal) and is well calibrated.
design: V1-V5: 240 matchups, 23,922 poss; V6: 520 matchups, 69,876 poss (season_engines); bias, MAE, RMSE, R2, win-side accuracy.
failure_evidence: At 520 matchups / 69,876 poss the signal is -0.12 pts/100 and R2 0.03.
notes: Treating positive prediction bias as 'validated signal' is conceptually flawed. V6 template text says 'it does: 47.5%' for an expected >50%, so the conclusion contradicts the number.

title: A5 player-routing and A5b defensive attention penalty
hypothesis: Routing possessions to each play type's best player adds value over A3, and survives defensive attention adaptation.
design: Calibration framework V4-V6; A5 vs A3 and A5b vs A5 signal in pts/100.
failure_evidence: Shrinks from +0.94 to +0.03 pts/100 on the larger 520-matchup sample.
notes: Model-scored, not observed outcomes.

title: Decision value test: kernel argmax vs NBA baseline (v1 leak, v2 fixed)
hypothesis: Kernel model A play-type recommendations add value over a league-adjusted baseline on holdout.
design: 23,922 scored holdout possessions; decision regret, value added per 100, calibration; v2 fixes oracle leakage and adds feasibility filter.
primary_result: v1: A -4.51 pts/100 vs baseline; v2: -1.48 pts/100, regret 0.1648 vs 0.1556, A outperforms in 9/240 matchups; recommendations ~88% CUT.
failure_evidence: Baseline wins on 23,922 possessions in both versions.
notes: v1 regret oracle used future (holdout) data; fixed in v2.

title: Usage-curve constrained optimizer (A2) vs baseline
hypothesis: Diminishing-returns usage curves improve recommendations over static argmax and baseline.
design: Same 23,922 holdout possessions; per-possession and distribution-level evaluation.
primary_result: A2 -8.32 pts/100 vs baseline; A2 vs A -6.84; A2 outperforms baseline 47/240. Distribution: A2 mix +13.40 pts/100 vs actual (beats 217/240) but -24.85 vs B argmax.
failure_evidence: -8.32 pts/100 vs baseline on 23,922 possessions.
notes: Doc labels -6.84 as an 'improvement'; number and wording disagree.

title: Evaluation-alignment diagnostic and opponent-strength lambda sweep
hypothesis: Equilibrium and actual-mix predictors explain matchup PPP better than simple means; opponent-strength scaling helps.
design: 520 holdout matchup cells, 69,876 poss; R2 vs global/team means; lambda 0-1.5 post-hoc sweep.
primary_result: Equilibrium R2 -0.1981; actual-mix R2 -0.7167; team-offense mean R2 +0.1197; >=100-poss cells equil -0.2785. Lambda sweep: R2 worsens monotonically (lambda 1.0 -0.2862).
failure_evidence: Both model predictors have negative R2 while team-mean is +0.1197; R2 more negative in larger cells.
notes: Opponent-strength adjustment, recommended as high-ROI, made it worse.

title: Alpha blend of actual-usage and equilibrium predictions
hypothesis: Blending equilibrium with actual-usage prediction beats either alone.
design: val 690 cells (84,319 poss), holdout 520 cells (69,876 poss); alpha sweep raw and OLS-calibrated.
primary_result: Best alpha = 1.00 (pure actual usage): R2 hol +0.0451 raw, +0.0672 calibrated; fullEQ R2 -0.1981.
failure_evidence: Best alpha ~1.0, meaning 'equilibrium is NOT predictive' per pre-written cheat sheet.

title: Blended prior-season shrinkage evaluator and k sweep
hypothesis: Blending prior seasons helps early season without hurting late season.
design: Fixed test 155 late-2024-25 games; current-only vs pooled vs blended (k=5,10,20,30); early-season simulation with 150 games.
primary_result: Late: blended k=30 worse on 5/5 metrics (R2 -0.1065 vs -0.0866). Early: blended better 5/5 (R2 -0.2624 vs -0.4508; win-side 55.8% vs 52.5%). k sweep recommends k~5.
failure_evidence: Early-season blend improves all 5 metrics, but all R2 remain negative.
notes: Supported only as relative improvement; absolute accuracy stays below a mean predictor.

title: Per-play-type interaction residual feature (Phase 1b)
hypothesis: Per-PT team-pair interaction deltas add R2 over the 8-feature baseline (ship if lift > +0.005).
design: 870 train cells (386,675 poss); shrinkage k sweep 25-1000; holdout R2.
primary_result: Best k=500 R2_hol +0.1192 vs +0.1150 baseline; lift +0.0042; w_pt negative (-1.4014).
failure_evidence: Lift +0.0042 < +0.005 ship threshold.
notes: Negative weight suggests overfitting sparse cells.

title: Alignment regression: shift toward engine recommendation vs series ORtg
hypothesis: Teams whose playoff mix shifted toward the engine's recommended PT have higher series ORtg residuals.
design: 68 (team, series) pairs; Pearson/Spearman, bootstrap CI, OLS with mix-shift control; provisional tuning/holdout split.
primary_result: Pearson r -0.032, CI [-0.283, +0.209]; Spearman -0.067; OLS beta -5.33 (SE 19.64); clean subset r -0.079 (n=54); tuning fold +0.135, holdout -0.125.
failure_evidence: n=68 with CI width ~0.49 on r; doc says sample thin.
notes: Conflicts with the CASE_STUDIES claim of a +3.3 ORtg alignment effect.

title: Agent sequential adaptation test (costly-hit / matchup-hit)
hypothesis: An LLM agent given possession sequences identifies costly PTs and the series-specific top net-swing PT.
design: 6 series-team units; agent output scored on costly-hit and matchup-hit.
primary_result: Parse 6/6; costly-hit 100%; matchup-hit 100%; CUT emphasized 6/6.
failure_evidence: n=6; agent emphasized CUT in 6/6, consistent with generic advice.
notes: Costly PTs are the same league-wide (77-88% of units), so the costly-hit benchmark is easy.

hypothesis: A generalist LLM (gemini-2.5-flash) on raw aggregates agrees with the engine and beats the team modal PT.
design: 3 (team, series) pairs scored.
primary_result: Pairs with both agent and engine recs: 0; agent scoreable n=0; engine hit 2/3 (66.7%).
failure_evidence: 0 agent recommendations produced; n=3.

title: Agent Test B: LLM counter selection vs deterministic BEST tier
hypothesis: The LLM picks the same counter as the BEST tier, and when it disagrees it is right in H2.
design: 3 suppression triggers; H2 PPP as referee.
primary_result: Agrees with BEST 1/3; picks AVOID 2/3; disagreements engine right 2/2; mean H2 PPP BEST 1.650, agent 1.154, AVOID 0.642.
failure_evidence: n=3 triggers; caveat says 230+ disagreements needed.

title: Agent Test C: 3-agent halftime debate vs optimizer counter
hypothesis: The LLM debate adds value over the deterministic optimizer counter.
design: 5 suppression triggers; agreement and H2 PPP when they disagree.
primary_result: Agreement 2/5 (40%); disagreements 3: debate wins 1, optimizer 1, tie 1; mean H2 PPP optimizer 1.812 vs debate 1.683.

title: Crunch-time identity stability year over year
hypothesis: Team crunch-time PPP delta vs baseline is a stable organizational identity.
design: 93 team-seasons 2022-25, gate >=100 crunch possessions; YoY Pearson across 62 pairs; player-attribution heuristic.
primary_result: YoY r = -0.023 (n=62 pairs); consistently positive CHI +0.056, CHA +0.040; negative NOP -0.074.
failure_evidence: r=-0.023 on 62 pairs; per-team-season crunch samples ~100+ possessions, so deltas of +/-0.05 PPP are within sampling noise.
notes: Doc still calls consistently positive teams 'genuine crunch-time performers' despite r~0, and has a blank team row. Knowable because single-season PPP on ~100 possessions has SE comparable to the deltas.

title: Play-type label backfill verification
hypothesis: Backfilled play-type labels match expected league distributions and team identities.
design: 921,514 labelled possessions; band tests on PT shares, PNR cap, PPP sanity, temporal distribution, team identity and directional checks.
primary_result: PNR 28.7% FAIL (band 20-28%); PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL; 3100 games with team PNR >33% FAIL; PNR PPP 0.948 PASS; temporal PASS; team identity FAIL; 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams. Final: FAIL.

notes: Report says do not run adaptation analysis until resolved.

title: Case studies: alignment with engine mix vs ORtg (+3.3 claim)
hypothesis: Games where the team mix was closest to the engine recommendation score more after strength adjustment.
design: 908 holdout game-team pairs; terciles of L1 distance; 6 illustrative cases with kernel unconstrained vs +/-5pp coachable vs calibrated (10-feature residual calibrator val R2 +0.1244) and 4 named-scheme robustness.
primary_result: Closest vs most-deviated tercile +3.3 ORtg adjusted (raw +5.2); Spearman rho >0.4 in 62% of games. Cases: GSW-LAL rho 1.00 coachable +28.0 ORtg; MIA-BOS rho 0.80 aligned residual +27.9; NYK-LAL rho 0.80 coachable +25.0; CLE-PHX rho -0.80; LAL-GSW rho 0.90 residual +12.3 despite deviation; MIN-DEN rho 0.10 L1=0.99 residual -29.8.
failure_evidence: No CI or test reported for +3.3; in-game PT ranking used as rho target shares outcome data; 3 of 6 cases are labeled honest counter-examples; every kernel rec is CUT-heavy.
notes: Contradicted by series-level alignment regression r=-0.032 (APPA-024). Coachable caps still +14.3 to +28.0 ORtg, which are model-internal not observed. Full file now read.

title: Execution conformance scoring ORL vs DET
hypothesis: Measure how closely each team executed the recommended opener.
design: One game, 2 offenses; leverage-weighted conformance scores.
primary_result: ORL avg leverage |d| 12.6pp, scores 86.3/87.4; DET 7.7pp, 82.3/92.3; DET matched opener #3.
notes: DET note says it 'nailed the high-leverage moves' while PULL_UP was +10.2pp over the recommendation.

title: Opener recommendations vs personnel feasibility
hypothesis: Rank-1 openers are within what the top-8 rotation can sustain.
design: 8 team-games from 4 playoff games; opener target share vs personnel capacity x1.25.
primary_result: 8/8 rank-1 openers CUT-centered and INFEASIBLE; worst gaps +9.6 to +15.9pp; CUT target 14-18% vs ceiling 2-6%.
failure_evidence: Optimizer ignores personnel; CUT target 3-10x stretch ceiling in every team-game.
notes: Explains the degenerate CUT-heavy recommendations seen in eval reports.

title: Opponent-relative leverage prevalence sweep
hypothesis: How often does an opponent-specific exploitable defensive weakness exist?
design: 870 ordered team pairs; defense PT edge vs league >= +5% on seed PTs.
primary_result: Exploit available 33.3%; trap 23.3%; both 6.7%; neither 50.0%; median best edge 3.79%.
notes: Edges depend only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), so they are not matchup-specific.

title: Relative-structure single-game validation BOS vs OKC
hypothesis: Model's top-ranked play types score above team average in a held-out game.
design: One holdout game 0022400946; Spearman of predicted vs actual PT PPP (PTs >=3 poss); top-3/bottom-3 hits.
primary_result: BOS rho 0.200, top-3 n/a, bottom-3 1/3; OKC rho 0.543, top-3 2/2, lift +0.308, bottom-3 1/3.
failure_evidence: One game; 5-6 PTs per team with 4-35 possessions.

title: Suppression tier ranking: BEST vs AVOID / BEST vs continue
hypothesis: After an H1 suppression trigger, BEST-tier counters score more in H2 than AVOID counters or continuing the suppressed play.
design: Triggers H1/H2 n>=5, drop >=0.25; 25-series (290 triggers), 55-series (633 triggers) and RS 2025-26 holdout (2,779 triggers); row-mean H2 PPP by tier.
primary_result: 25-series BEST-AVOID +0.581, MW p=5.16e-24; 55-series ungated +0.548, n-gated +0.375; BEST vs continue +0.445 PO / +0.584 RS; robustness: CUT removed +0.279, n>=10 +0.221, within-PT fixed effects +0.100; RS Spearman -0.344; INSUFF 55.7-57.3% of rows.
failure_evidence: Gap survives the leakage fix but shrinks to +0.100 with within-play-type fixed effects.
notes: Pre-fix leaky gap ~+0.488 and the 25-series sample was not rerun after the Scout leakage fix. BEST is what teams actually ran (selection effect).

title: Suppression is not regression to mean: matched-control excess
hypothesis: The H1-to-H2 PPP drop after a trigger exceeds the drop of a matched control, beyond what RTM predicts.
design: Playoff 55-series: 633 triggers, opponent same-PT same-game control (534 pairs) plus EB shrinkage. Full graph then H1-PPP-balanced caliper match, cluster-robust by game, blowout filter; Z1 OT exclusion and Z2 c_h2_n>=5 applied 2026-07-11.
failure_evidence: Excess drops from +0.625 unconstrained to +0.408 when balanced on H1 PPP, but the cluster CI excludes 0; Z1+Z2 moved excess only +0.004 vs pre-fix +0.404.
power_info: 848 game clusters, eff. n ~1,088; PO 534 pairs
notes: Deck slide 3 still cites legacy +0.628 / n=9,900. Code audit Z1 (OT in H2, 4,674 poss) and Z2 (control c_h2_n unconstrained) were HIGH severity and then corrected in the paper-locked numbers. Shrinkage excess +0.495 (80%) recommended off the slide.

title: Fragility F1: usage-residual structural load exists and is split-half stable
hypothesis: On the full sample, usage explains <90% of structural load with residual share CI lower bound >0.10 (F1a), and usage-residual load is split-half stable (F1b pooled and usage-partial).
design: 120 team-seasons, 30 franchises; fragility_full_study.py --n-null 500 --n-perm 5000 seed 17 N_BOOT=2000; franchise-clustered permutation and bootstrap. Amendment 1 (post-gate, pre-full-run) made usage-partial Spearman co-primary for F1b.
primary_result: F1a cosine R2=0.094, residual-share=0.906, CI [0.768, 0.962] PASS; Frobenius R2=0.073 share=0.927 CI [0.828, 0.965]. F1b pooled-residual rho=+0.685 p=0.0000 CI [+0.649, +0.721]; usage-partial rho=+0.557 p=0.0000 CI [+0.491, +0.618].
failure_evidence: Residual-share CI lower bound 0.768 > registered 0.10; both F1b CIs exclude 0 and p<0.01; 30 franchises above the ~20 floor.
power_info: 120 team-seasons, 30 franchises; 1962 season-level players; 1965 paired players
notes: One allowed mid-course correction: usage-partial F1b co-primary because usage itself is split-half stable. Load is registered as not a value/points measure.

title: Cost of ignoring suppression: continue rate and points lost
hypothesis: After a suppression trigger, teams keep running the suppressed play at near-H1 volume and lose several points per event.
design: 55-series graph; Group A h2_n>=3 vs Group B h2_n<=1; within-game H1 vs H2 on suppressed PT; points decomposition via _points_not_ppp.py. RS confirm _rs_continue_rate.py.
primary_result: PO: 735 events; Group A 683 (93%) H1 1.522 to H2 0.876, cost/poss 0.646, ~8.2 H2 poss, ~97% H1 volume, ~5.4 pts/trigger; real actionable ~6.1 pts (5.3 keep-calling + 0.8 AVOID vs BEST). RS continue 93.1% (2,949/3,169); no-floor 94.1%.
failure_evidence: 93% continue at ~97% of H1 volume; blowout-filtering continue rate is a volume-threshold artifact (78.8% at |margin|<=20) so the paper cites unfiltered 93%/94.9%.
power_info: 683 Group A PO triggers; 3,169 RS events
notes: H1 PPP floor=1.0 in cost/continue scripts but not in the trigger table; removing it changes continue 94.9% to 94.1%. Oracle ceiling 11.1 pts is labeled projection.

title: Post-trigger pickup toward BEST and alignment vs series wins
hypothesis: After suppression, teams shift H2 mix toward BEST-tier counters, and running BEST (vs AVOID) predicts series wins.
design: 55 series, 272 games, 633 triggers, 110 series-directions; H1 to H2 BEST/AVOID share pickup; Spearman of %BEST/%AVOID vs series won.
primary_result: 591/633 triggers with BEST defined: 51.6% shifted more toward BEST, 22.4% used more AVOID; avg best_pickup +0.0024 pp; BEST share 10.0% to 10.2%; AVOID 8.9% to 9.5%. %BEST vs won rho=+0.131 p=0.17 n=110; %AVOID vs won rho=-0.098 p=0.31. H2 mix BEST 11.3% / AVOID 7.8% / INSUFF 55.8% volume.
failure_evidence: Average BEST pickup ~0; alignment vs winning not significant at n=110. Teams already run ~29% AVOID in H1.
notes: IND counterexample: 18.6% BEST follow, 71.4% series win rate (7 series-directions). Pickup is the behavioral claim; alignment is a second test in the same coaching section.

title: Suppression vs routing: defense reads play type not initiator
hypothesis: The H2 PPP collapse after a trigger is initiator-specific (routing) rather than play-type suppression; swapping the primary initiator should recover efficiency.
design: RS 2025-26 holdout 2,779 triggers; same-player both-halves pairs; same vs swapped primary initiator; _test_same_vs_swap.py. Prevalence: 1,783/2,296 processed team-games (77.7%) or 72.5% vs full-season denominator.
primary_result: Deck baseline drop 0.631 (H1 1.470 to H2 0.839, n=2,779). Same player both halves drop 0.643 (n=10,194 pairs). Same initiator 825 drop 0.575/0.600; swapped 1,732 drop 0.634/0.639; SWAP-SAME +0.039 p=0.002 d=0.12. 68% swap. Routing regret on BEST counter poss +0.116 PPP, 72.4% oracle wins, n=6,808 (sheet also cites +0.124).
failure_evidence: Same-player drop 0.643 matches the play-type drop 0.631; swapping initiator does not recover (swap drop 0.639, replacement 1.093 vs demoted 0.789).
notes: Doc verdict: kill routing-regret as an adaptation mechanism on suppressed H2 plays; keep routing regret on BEST counter possessions. Cite-now line says +0.124; related-behavioral table says +0.116.

title: Counter play-type matchup specificity (Rank step)
hypothesis: Given the same defense, different offenses get different BEST counters, and knowing the suppressed PT reduces counter entropy.
design: RS holdout; _counter_specificity.py and _counter_matchup_specificity.py; entropy of BEST counters.
primary_result: Median entropy 1.543 (mostly matchup-specific). Knowing suppressed PT reduces entropy -0.344 (within-PT 1.331). One offense vs different defenses mixed: BOS/MIA/OKC vary; LAL/TOR often one counter.
failure_evidence: No inferential test on the entropy values; mixed identity vs matchup pattern across teams.
notes: Supports Rank as partly matchup-informed; ~80% of BEST counters are still the generic best (W4).

title: Oracle player matchup specificity on BEST counters (Route step)
hypothesis: The oracle BEST player for a counter play type varies by opponent, not a single team identity.
design: _oracle_player_specificity.py; n=6,852 oracle BEST possessions; (off_team, play_type) cells.
primary_result: 64/78 (82%) (off, PT) cells have >1 oracle player across opponents; 19/78 dominated by one player (>=90%); median oracle-player entropy 0.928.
failure_evidence: 82% of cells vary the oracle player by opponent.
notes: Valid on counter plays only; routing on suppressed plays was rejected in APPA-042.

title: Joint vs sequential Rank-then-Route ranking
hypothesis: Picking play type and player jointly beats sequential Rank then Route enough to justify the extra step.
design: _joint_vs_sequential.py; n=2,779 RS triggers; blended matchup PPP, min 3 H2H poss/player.
primary_result: Joint pick = sequential 80.3%; joint reroutes 19.7% (547). Mean PPP left on table +0.020 all / +0.099 reroutes only (median +0.080). Play-type gap BEST vs 2nd 0.215 mean / 0.182 median. Routing premium +0.089. Strict dominance 49.2%.
failure_evidence: Mean +0.020 PPP left on table is small; sequential declared safe ~80% with joint tiebreak in ~20%.
notes: Prior weight 50 ? reroutes partly reflect talent routing, not pure matchup.

title: Adaptation vs generic counter (W4)
hypothesis: BEST-tier counters are suppression-specific rather than the team's generic best available play.
design: _adaptation_vs_generic.py; n=1,539 RS triggers with BEST tier + viable blended PPP (55.4% of 2,779).
primary_result: BEST == generic best 78.3%; suppression-specific 21.7%. Defense suppressed generic-best 4.7% (73); then specific 39.7%. When supp != generic, still picks generic 79.2%. (off,def) counter changes by what was suppressed 48.8% (190/389). PNR adapt 28.3% n=428; PULL_UP 28.5% n=291. True INSUFF (no valid counter) 0/11,087 full-graph triggers.
failure_evidence: 78.3% of ranked BEST counters are the generic best available; Rank adds value in ~20-22%, 39.7% when defense took the team's best.
power_info: n=1,539 W4 triggers; 1,466 (95.3%) had a better option already
notes: Deck '80%' and '1,600 triggers' should be 78.3% and 1,539. Pivot remains counterfactual: 93% do not pivot. Drop magnitude does not predict smarter counters (~22% flat).

title: Live H2 trigger timing: remaining possessions window
hypothesis: Suppression can be detected live in H2 with enough possessions remaining to act.
design: Live H2 trigger simulation _run_live_trigger_validation.py; cited only as mean remaining possessions in the paper-mapping table.
primary_result: Mean 21 poss remaining.
failure_evidence: Sheet records only the mean (~21); no distribution, hit rate, or comparison to a false-alarm rate in this file.
notes: Primary artifact live_trigger_report.md is outside this slice.

title: Player-level BEST vs AVOID H2 PPP gaps (exploratory)
hypothesis: Players score more on BEST-ranked counters than AVOID-ranked counters in the 55-series playsheets.
design: 55-series graph; each player BEST-tier vs AVOID-tier H2 PPP; min 5 rows per tier; N=78 players.
primary_result: 78 players with >=5 BEST and >=5 AVOID rows. Top gaps D. Lively II +1.833 (n=6/6), M. Brogdon +1.831 (7/11); some reverse (N. Jokic -0.333 n=8/18; L. Doncic -0.190 n=6/14). Stars mixed (D. White +0.864 n=49/42; SGA +0.333 n=5/60).
failure_evidence: n is small for most players (single-game playsheets); no multiplicity or clustered test.
notes: Exploratory; sheet says n is small for most players.

title: Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock (8/8 PTs)
hypothesis: After the opponent runs play type X, the next offensive play type Y scores above Y's unconditional H2 baseline, and every PT has a defensive aftershock.
design: own_seq_ec; n=458,604 opp possessions; all-games vs playoffs split; premium = Y PPP after X vs Y H2 baseline.
primary_result: A2 aftershock 8/8 PTs replicate all-games and playoffs (CUT +0.119 n=21,398 / PO +0.131 n=1,145 through TRANSITION +0.135 n=26,262 / +0.126 n=1,529). Top pair premiums: PUTBACK->TRANSITION +0.084 n=565; CUT->PULL_UP +0.065 n=2,620.
failure_evidence: 8/8 play types replicate in both all-games and playoffs.
notes: Team-level 1-2 punch table includes tiny-n cells (BKN n=16, CHI n=18) marked sig at |t|>=2.0.

title: Superstar sequential suppression: opponent play before the star
hypothesis: A specific opponent play type on the preceding possession suppresses each star's next-possession PPP relative to that star's baseline.
design: Full graph RS+PO; 30 stars; min n=30 after the suppressor PT.
primary_result: PUTBACK is top suppressor for 6+ stars (e.g. D. Mitchell 1.178 to 0.884, d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345 n=32; C. Holmgren d=-0.222 n=52). Other tops: TRANSITION (A. Davis -0.058), POST_UP (N. Jokic -0.075), PULL_UP (A. Edwards -0.043).
failure_evidence: No multiplicity correction; n_after is 32-95 for several PUTBACK cells vs thousands of baseline possessions.
notes: PUTBACK as a league-wide suppressor is the claim later tested as a mechanism in APPA-054/055.

title: Season adapter profiles: BEST-share vs playoff winning
hypothesis: Teams that consistently run more BEST-tier counters across seasons win more playoff series-directions.
design: 55-series, 4 seasons; team BEST%/AVOID% and Win% by series-direction.
primary_result: Top BEST-share: BOS 15.7%/AVOID 21.4% Win 70% (10 dirs, 4 seasons); LAL 15.5%/23.1% Win 50% (6); OKC 12.3%/18.6% Win 89% (9 dirs, 3 seasons). Chronic AVOID: ORL 8.5%/59.3% Win 0% (3 dirs, 3 seasons).
failure_evidence: Descriptive team table; no test. Alignment vs winning already n.s. at n=110 (APPA-041). ORL n=3 series-dirs.
notes: OKC called out as third-highest BEST share and 89% win rate; talent confound untested here.

title: CUT feasibility cap: BEST-AVOID gap without CUT-heavy games
hypothesis: The BEST vs AVOID gap is inflated by games where CUT exceeds 15% of H2 mix.
design: 55-series trigger table + Neo4j H2 mix; exclude games with CUT share >15%.
primary_result: All games BEST 1.473 vs AVOID 0.853 gap +0.620 MW p=0.0000 Spearman -0.316 n=2,544. CUT<=15%: +0.625 n=2,508. CUT>15%: +0.163 n.s. n=36. Only 4/272 games had CUT>15%.
failure_evidence: Removing the 4 CUT-heavy games slightly strengthens the gap (+0.620 to +0.625).
notes: This uses the ungated +0.620 55-series gap (stale relative to n-gated +0.375 / BEST-vs-continue +0.445). Robustness direction still holds on this CSV.

title: Player and teammate sequential premiums
hypothesis: Specific same-player and teammate X->Y sequences carry PPP premiums above Y's baseline.
design: Full graph; min n=30; same initiator vs different initiator on Y.
primary_result: Top same-player: P. George DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.560 n=31 t=+2.2; J. Brown +0.349 n=62; L. Doncic DRIVE->PNR +0.309 n=53. Top teammate: K. Towns->O. Anunoby DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.398 n=30; J. Brown->J. Tatum DRIVE->PNR +0.326 n=43.
failure_evidence: Min n=30 cells; several labeled DIRECTIONAL at t~2.1-2.2; no multiplicity correction.
notes: DRIVE->SPOT_UP and DRIVE->PNR dominate the top list.

title: PUTBACK suppression mechanism: fatigue vs value
hypothesis: PUTBACK suppresses the next star possession via fatigue (stronger in H2 and Q4), while PUTBACK itself remains high-value.
design: Four tests on PUTBACK-suppressed stars: H1 vs H2 delta, Q1 vs Q4, PUTBACK H2 PPP vs baseline, offense PPP after opp PUTBACK.
failure_evidence: Q4 PUTBACK is sparse (34 pooled poss at n>=30; Mitchell n=34 drives the Q4 cell) even though the H2 vs H1 and aftershock tests are larger.
power_info: 22 stars H1+H2; Q4 pooled n=34; 15,898 aftershock poss
notes: Sheet calls fatigue the primary driver; Q4 sparsity is knowable from the n>=30 gate.

title: All play types x Q1-Q4 gradient on 30 stars
hypothesis: Only PUTBACK shows a fatigue signature (near-zero Q1 suppression compounding to Q4) across the full 30-star panel.
design: Possession-weighted league delta of star PPP vs own-quarter baseline; no n floor; 30 stars x 9 opp PTs.
primary_result: PUTBACK Q1 d=-0.001 to Q4 d=-0.233, Q1->Q4 -0.232 (Q1 poss 722 / Q4 531). Other PTs suppress in Q1 already; largest other gradient DRIVE -0.060. CUT reverses +0.020. TRANSITION -0.053.
failure_evidence: On the full 30-star weighted panel, only PUTBACK is near-zero in Q1 and heavy in Q4.
notes: Section Q n>=30 gate gave Q1 -0.009 to Q4 -0.289; no-floor weighted gives the same qualitative story.

title: TRANSITION gradient subgroup on four pace-sensitive stars
hypothesis: For stars whose #1 sequential suppressor is TRANSITION (Tatum, Morant, Young, Haliburton), TRANSITION hits hardest in Q1 then adapts by Q4, unlike PUTBACK.
design: 4-player cluster; min n=15 per player-quarter cell.
primary_result: TRANSITION Q1 d=-0.221 (n=352) to Q4 d=-0.146 (n=262), gradient +0.075. PUTBACK compounds -0.067; POST_UP compounds -0.098. T. Young exception Q1 -0.023 to Q4 -0.240.
failure_evidence: 4-star subgroup selected on the outcome (TRANSITION is already their #1 suppressor); full 30-star TRANSITION gradient is only -0.053.
power_info: 4 stars; TRANSITION Q1 n=352 / Q4 n=262
notes: Sheet says do not cite these numbers as the full 30-star league average.

title: Double-suppression stacking (POST_UP then PUTBACK)
hypothesis: Opponent POST_UP then PUTBACK stacks additively against the next star possession.
design: League sequence opp POST_UP -> offense -> opp PUTBACK -> star next; vs each alone. Mitchell PUTBACK-by-opponent directional split.
primary_result: Baseline 1.210 n=960,764. After PUTBACK only 1.097 d=-0.113 n=15,898. After POST_UP only 1.091 d=-0.119 n=76,329. Stacked 1.138 d=-0.071 n=1,047 vs additive prediction -0.232. Mitchell after PUTBACK 0.919 vs 1.252 (d=-0.333, n=95); 8/13 teams below baseline n>=5, spread 1.200 PPP.
failure_evidence: Stacked suppression -0.071 is less than either alone and far below additive -0.232 (n=1,047).
notes: Shared-pathway interpretation: offense adjusts after the first disruption.

title: Season stability of top suppressors and negative teammate pairs
hypothesis: Each star's top sequential suppressor is stable across seasons, and some teammate X->Y sequences have large negative premiums.
design: 30 stars x 4 seasons; min n=20 per player-season-opp_play cell. Negative pairs: premium < -0.10, n>=30.
primary_result: 2/30 (7%) stable (>=75% same top suppressor): D. Mitchell PUTBACK 75%, L. James POST_UP 75%. Negative: J. Tatum->K. Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444 n=31; Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263 n=31; J. Brown->J. Tatum SPOT_UP->DRIVE -0.186 n=37.
failure_evidence: Only 2/30 stars meet the 75% same-top-suppressor stability rule.
notes: Positive counterpart Brown DRIVE -> Tatum PNR +0.326 n=43; sequence type matters more than pairing.

title: Historical upset backtest: V2 P(overperform) on 4 known series
hypothesis: V2 P(overperform) plus the top-feasible opener recovers the narrative lever of four known playoff upsets without future leakage.
design: 4 series; leakage-safe RS priors (playoff games of the target year dropped); calibration off; 7-game binomial rollup. Tempo mix from pooled within-team-season regression n=9,830 team-games.
primary_result: Lever fired 1/4 (DAL-OKC matchup_hunt_stack YES). MIA-MIL: V1 series 0.1% / V2 post-opener 8.7%, top TOV_AVOID not variance_push. IND-NYK: 25.6% vs 44.9%, top TOV_AVOID not tempo UP. ORL-CLE: 45.8% vs 65.2%, top TOV_AVOID not personnel_feasibility. DAL-OKC: 34.6% vs 52.1%, top TOV_FORCE; matchup_hunt_stack was #2 (P=50.5%). TEMPO UP for MIA dP -0.5pp; TEMPO DOWN +0.6pp.
failure_evidence: n=4 selected known upsets; expected lever matched in 1/4; all top-feasible openers collapsed to four-factor TOV/OREB rather than the claimed mechanism except DAL's #2.
notes: OREB_PUSH was top-5 for every series with realized muDelta +0.012 to +0.015 and a fixed 0.55 survival ratio. Earlier TEMPO_UP for MIA (+0.7pp) was a hand-picked mix-shift term.

title: PT-shift layer diagnostic across four upset series
hypothesis: The play-type mix optimizer produces different feasible destination PTs by matchup (prescriptive) rather than one universal clipped destination (diagnostic).
design: Same 4 leakage-safe series; top feasible PT-shift destination, ceiling vs aspirational pp, muDelta.
primary_result: No feasible PT shift in any of 4 series. Distinct top-feasible destination PTs: 0 (none).
failure_evidence: 0/4 series surfaced a feasible PT shift; verdict 'Confirmed diagnostic, not prescriptive.' Continuous feasibility still collapses away from a matchup-specific opener.
notes: Knowable from the CUT-everywhere / personnel-feasibility failure (APPA-033).

title: L5 ablation: deterministic V4 vs LangGraph agent V5
hypothesis: LangGraph agents (V5) improve play-type recommendations over the deterministic engine (V4).
design: 20 series, 40 paired (slug, side) observations; 2,000 series-cluster bootstrap; Holm-Bonferroni on Wilcoxon regret and McNemar.
primary_result: Median regret V4 0.102 [0.067, 0.128] vs V5 0.067 [0.050, 0.100], Holm p=0.062. V5 beats V4 11/40 vs 4/40, McNemar p=0.118. Override 8/40 (20%); override hit rate 25.0% [0.000, 1.000]. Brittle precision 7.5%. Parse 40/40. Runtime 60.1s vs 349.6s (5.816x).
failure_evidence: Holm p=0.062 and McNemar p=0.118 on n=40; override hit 25% on 8 overrides; 0 player-level overrides scorable.
notes: Doc interpretation 'AGENTS DEGRADE QUALITY' is stronger than the tests (neither primary p<0.05 after Holm). Successful-override table lists only 2 rows with V5 rec='none'.

title: L5 baseline comparison: V0/V2/V4/V5 team-aggregate regret
hypothesis: Scheme fingerprint (V2), optimizer (V4), and agents (V5) beat a scheme-neutral team PPP baseline on |projected-observed| regret.
design: Same 40 (slug, side) pairs from l5_ablation_results.parquet; observed_ppp is series-level weighted-mean PPP, not per-recommendation.
primary_result: Mean regret: V0_NEUTRAL 0.1072, V0_TEAM 0.1053, V2_TEAM 0.1003, V4 0.1148, V5 0.0979. V2 vs V0_NEUTRAL mean_diff -0.0069 p=0.190. V4 vs V0_NEUTRAL +0.0075 p=0.563 (V4 worse). V5 vs V4 n_diff=15 beat_rate 0.275 / cond 0.733 mean_diff -0.0169 p=0.0309. V5 vs V0_NEUTRAL -0.0093 p=0.2589.
failure_evidence: n=40; V2 and full stack vs neutral p>0.05; V4 trends worse than neutral. Only V5 vs V4 on 15 differing pairs is p=0.031.
notes: Conflicts with APPA-061 'AGENTS DEGRADE' headline: here V5 median/mean regret is lower than V4. Target is team-aggregate PPP, not the recommended play type.

title: Holdout play-type rank validation (LAYER_AUDIT)
hypothesis: Pre-game PT PPP ranking from training data correlates with actual efficiency ranking in held-out games.
design: Train 523,517 possession sequences; 454 holdout games; 908 (game, team) rows; Spearman of predicted vs actual PT rank (PTs >=3 poss, >=4 common PTs); top-3 hit/lift; bottom-3 suppression.
primary_result: Median rho +0.539 (IQR +0.245 to +0.750); 62.4% rho>0.4; 88.4% rho>0; 10.5% rho<0. Top-3 median hit 100%; >=2/3 hits 78.9%; median lift +0.4261 PPP; 90.8% positive lift. Bottom-3 median suppression 66.7%. MAE cited in later reports 0.0922 PPP.
failure_evidence: Doc caveat: top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency PTs (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION); 10.5% of rows the model misleads (rho<0).
notes: This is the Spearman 0.54 recycled in generated TEAM_vs_TEAM reports. Team medians range NOP +0.727 to WAS +0.341.

title: G5 blog replay: LP opener vs realized mix SAS-OKC
hypothesis: The LP-equilibrium opener (CUT) and AVOID (PNR) match realized efficiency in WCF Game 5 SAS @ OKC (0042500315).
design: One game scored post hoc against historical H2H baselines (replay uses PlayTypeInferrer + PNR proxy). Live blog is the in-game feed of the same game.
primary_result: Final SAS 114-OKC 127. SAS CUT 9 poss 1.67 vs H2H 1.59 CORRECT; SAS PNR 22 poss 0.95 vs 0.94 MIXED (LP AVOID). OKC CUT 1 poss 2.00 vs 1.69 CORRECT but 1% mix vs plan. OKC PNR 19 poss 1.26 vs 1.11 (AVOID but above H2H). Live: both teams ~65-71% PULL_UP, CUT 1-5%.
failure_evidence: One game; CUT opener was high-PPP on tiny volume (SAS n=9, OKC n=1) while both teams ran PULL_UP as the modal PT.
notes: Live blog has no post-game accuracy table; the scored assessment is only in G5_BLOG_REPLAY.md.

title: Freeform agent sequential demo: MIA vs BOS 2023 G7
hypothesis: An agent given only possession sequences can recover a conditional decision tree and series-level adaptation in one high-stakes game.
design: One Game 7 (0042200307); MIA 75 poss in thirds of 25; Markov-1 after make/miss; BOS next-PPP aftershock; 7-game PT table.
primary_result: MIA thirds ORtg 108.0 / 136.0 / 156.0. After missed PNR (n=10) next PULL_UP 40%. POST_UP aftershock: BOS next-PPP 1.40 (miss n=5) and 1.50 (make n=4) vs PULL_UP make 0.00 (n=5). G4 POST_UP 0.40; G6 PNR 0.60; G7 PNR volume 10 to 18, PPP 0.60 to 1.06.
failure_evidence: Most tree cells n=3-10; doc states branches are hypotheses until validated across series.
notes: Demo explicitly does not claim engine recovery (separate Test A). Series score G7 103-84 MIA in Boston.

title: TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on four playoff games
hypothesis: TOV_FORCE as a top-3 lever can be decomposed into defender x initiator x PT channels with positive matchup lift.
design: 4 games (ORL-DET, PHI-BOS, PHX-OKC, POR-SAS); Dean-Oliver additive lift from 1.05M recency-weighted possessions; defender cell n>=15.
primary_result: Team-PT lifts are small (ORL vs DET PNR +1.2pp; POR vs SAS all PT lifts negative, e.g. PNR -4.1pp) while player-channel lifts are large on small n (Banchero on Huerter SPOT_UP +8.4pp, n_def=17 / n_off=54; Dort on Coffey SPOT_UP +12.0pp, n=25/16; Booker on Wiggins PULL_UP +14.8pp).
failure_evidence: Player-channel n often 15-28 defensive possessions; primary_defender attribution includes helper steals; no holdout or game-outcome check.
notes: POR vs SAS team-level lifts are all negative, so the top-3 TOV_FORCE lever is coming from sparse player cells, not team PT rates.

title: TOV_FORCE 3-ply adversarial surviving lift
hypothesis: Raw R1 TOV-force channel lifts survive opponent re-route or PT-shift (R2) and our follow-the-ball counter (R3).
design: Same 4 games; opponent min over re-route (top-3 alts) and PT-shift (>=200 opp poss); net surviving lift after R3. Direct cell if n>=10 else additive surrogate.
primary_result: R1 lifts shrink ~50%+: ORL Banchero/Huerter +8.4 to net +3.7pp; DET Green/Anthony +7.0 to +3.5; PHI Harris/Vucevic +12.0 to +6.0; BOS Holiday/Council +6.1 to +2.8; PHX Booker/Wiggins +14.8 to +7.5; OKC Dort/Coffey +12.0 to +5.8; POR Lillard/McLaughlin +5.2 to +2.6; SAS Jones/Wesley +10.3 to +4.6. Many R3 cells used n<10 surrogates.
failure_evidence: Net lift is model-implied, not observed in the games; R3 often additive surrogate at n<10.
notes: R2 is almost always re-route (not PT-shift) because shifting 20% of mix leaves 80% of the R1 channel intact.

title: Game retrospective template preview OKC vs PHX (unpopulated)
hypothesis: Pre-game vs halftime vs post-game pipeline runs on OKC-PHX Game 1 can be compared to observed stats.
design: Template for three temporal windows; intended to use ObservedGameStats and MatchupState. Train sequences listed as 0.
primary_result: All sections [MODELED pending] / [DELTA pending] / [OBSERVED pending]. Spearman 0.54 and MAE 0.0922 are copied from the holdout rank study, not computed here.
failure_evidence: Pipeline runs were never supplied; 0 possession sequences in the train split field.
notes: Placeholder preview, not a completed retrospective.

title: Play-type mix alignment vs actual PPP (matchup residual)
hypothesis: Holdout games where a team's play-type mix is closer to the model's recommended mix score more efficiently.
design: 908 holdout game-team rows (454 games), terciles of L1 distance actual vs recommended mix; actual PPP residualized on team offense and opponent defense means.
primary_result: Raw gap aligned-deviated +5.18 ORtg; strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg (+0.0193 vs -0.0134 PPP residual). Model regret median +25.94 ORtg (non-negative by construction).
failure_evidence: Strength-controlled gap +3.27 ORtg persists after team/opponent residualization.
notes: Observational; doc states regret is a tautology. _new/_prior files are identical reruns (only elapsed time differs).

title: Top-player on/off features in calibrator
hypothesis: Adding star on/off presence features (top-1 or top-3 players) improves holdout R2 over shipped 8-feature OLS.
design: Train-learned on/off deltas per top-N player, swept k_player shrinkage; val 690 cells, holdout 520 cells; compare R2_hol to 8-feat baseline +0.1150.
primary_result: top_n=3 best R2_hol +0.0971 (lift -0.0179); top_n=1 best R2_hol +0.0865 (lift -0.0285).
failure_evidence: Holdout lift negative at every k (-0.0179 / -0.0285).

title: Residual calibration A/B (global/linear/OLS/per-team)
hypothesis: A residual calibrator fit on VAL improves out-of-sample R2 of the equilibrium matchup evaluator.
design: Blended A3 evaluator trained on 523,517 sequences; calibrators fit on VAL (690 cells), scored on HOLDOUT (520 cells); with and without 30-game recency half-life.
primary_result: Holdout R2 baseline -0.1981 -> OLS +0.0323 (net lift +0.2305); HL30 variant baseline -0.1587 -> OLS +0.0321. Per-team R2 val +0.2449 but holdout +0.0213.
failure_evidence: OLS holdout R2 +0.0323 vs baseline -0.1981.
notes: Absolute R2 remains ~0.03; per-team calibrator overfits val (0.24 -> 0.02).

title: Calibration variance diagnostic (matchup signal collapse)
hypothesis: The calibrated pipeline preserves enough variance and the matchup model pred_raw carries usable signal.
design: 690 val / 520 holdout cells: variance ratios, slope test, drop-one and single-feature ablation, residual structure.
primary_result: pred_cal variance 3.9% of actual; pred_raw alone R2 +0.0042; dropping pred_raw changes R2 by +0.0002; team_mult alone +0.0392.
failure_evidence: pred_raw contributes ~0 (dR2 +0.0002); SHRINKAGE_SWEEP later showed the equilibrium optimizer collapses signal (R2 +0.004 vs +0.045 with actual usage).

title: Matchup-model shrinkage K sweep
hypothesis: Lowering SHRINKAGE_K in MatchupPPPModel recovers signal lost to over-shrinkage.
design: Sweep k=5..5000 on 690 val / 520 holdout cells using actual usage mix; R2 raw and OLS-calibrated on holdout.
primary_result: Hypothesis REJECTED: k=5 R2 alone +0.018, k=50 +0.045, k=200 +0.058; best OLS R2 +0.0744 at k=500 (lift +0.0072 vs k=50). Actual-usage path R2 +0.045 vs equilibrium path +0.004.
failure_evidence: Lower k gives wider spread but lower R2 (k=5 +0.018 vs k=200 +0.058).
notes: Byproduct finding: downstream equilibrium optimizer eats the matchup signal (10x).

title: Starter-share features in calibrator
hypothesis: Offensive/defensive starter-share features improve holdout R2.
design: Add 2 OLS features (top-5 by train possessions) to shipped 6-feat calibrator; val 690 / holdout cells.
failure_evidence: Lift +0.0315 > +0.01 ship threshold.
notes: Ship threshold stated in doc.

title: Shot-quality (xPPP, team shot-making) features
hypothesis: Shot-zone expected PPP and team shot-making skill add signal beyond box-score features.
design: Add xPPP and team make-skill features to 8-feat OLS; holdout R2.
primary_result: Best +xPPP only R2_hol +0.1204 (lift +0.0054); shot-skills -0.0003.
failure_evidence: Lift +0.0054 below the +0.02 'real signal' threshold (doc: mostly absorbed).

title: Final feature stacking ceiling

L2 MIA disagrees with L1 on DRIVE (L2 best=PNR not CUT, gap=+0.125), PNR (DRIVE not TRANSITION), POST_UP, PULL_UP, SPOT_UP. title: SQ2 decision quality hit rate: engine top pt_shift vs team modal PT
hypothesis: The V4 engine's recommended play type outperforms the team's highest-volume play type in that playoff series.

title: Ranked playsheet validation, 10 series (Spearman null; pairwise BEST>AVOID)
hypothesis: When a defense drops a play type >=0.25 PPP H1 to H2, playsheet counter ranking predicts which alternative scored better in H2 (BEST > SECOND > AVOID).
design: 10 completed 2025-26 playoff series; 665 counter observations / 142 unique triggers; Spearman of tier rank vs observed H2 PPP plus Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney BEST vs AVOID.

title: Cost of ignoring suppression (continue suppressed PT in H2)
hypothesis: When a suppression trigger fires and teams keep running the suppressed play type, H2 PPP on that PT is materially below H1.
design: 735 suppression events, 271 games; Group A h2_n>=3 (n=683) vs Group B h2_n<=1 (n=31). Canonical deck uses trigger CSV H1/H2 n>=5 (633 PO / 2779 RS).
primary_result: Group A: H1 1.522 -> post-trigger 0.876, cost 0.646 PPP/poss, 5.16 pts/trigger (t=48.172, p=0.0000, n=683). Pivot vs continue overall H2 1.074 vs 1.043, MW p=0.2642. Locked row-mean (n>=5): H1 1.48->H2 0.85, drop 0.63, 5.4 pts/trigger, n=633 PO / 2779 RS; full-graph drop 0.619 (n=11087).
failure_evidence: One-sample t on (h1-h2) p=0.0000 n=683; pivoting overall-H2 advantage not significant (p=0.2642, n_B=31).
power_info: n=683 Group A; n=31 Group B underpowered for pivot vs continue
notes: Do not cite poss-weighted cost 0.646 on slides; locked methodology is trigger row-mean drop 0.63. Win rates 48.8% vs 48.4% are indistinguishable.

title: System BEST vs constrained league mix (non-CUT matchup-specificity test)
hypothesis: Matchup-specific (non-CUT) BEST counters beat a feasibility-weighted league mix that ignores game state.
design: 633 triggers, 55 series. A=BEST counter; B=constrained mix (SPOT_UP 35%/PULL_UP 25%/CUT 15%/DRIVE 9%/PNR 8%/POST_UP 8%); C=naive pivot; D=AVOID. One-sided MW A>B.
primary_result: All BEST vs mix: 1.481 vs 1.212, gap=+0.269, p=0.0000, n=283. Non-CUT BEST vs mix: 1.216 vs 1.206, gap=+0.010, p=0.1709, n=136. L3_MATCHUP non-CUT: gap=+0.001, p=0.3277, n=47. BEST vs AVOID gap=+0.692, p=0.0000, n=169. 147/283 BEST are CUT (51.9%).
failure_evidence: Key non-CUT test gap=+0.010, p=0.1709, n=136; H2H L3 non-CUT gap=+0.001, p=0.3277. Headline A vs B is CUT-driven.
notes: Knowable: CUT is both 52% of BEST and in the constrained mix at 15%, so all-BEST vs mix cannot isolate matchup intelligence. Authors reframed contribution as trigger timing, not counter-selection.

title: DRIVE-as-BEST counter vs constrained mix
hypothesis: When BEST=DRIVE (counter_h2_n>=5), observed DRIVE H2 PPP beats a feasibility-constrained baseline.
design: 44 qualifying triggers, 39 games, 13 teams. Mix weights CUT 15%/SPOT_UP 35%/DRIVE 30%/OTHER 20%. One-sided MW A>B and A>C.
primary_result: A mean=1.178 vs B_game 1.236 (gap=-0.058, p=0.6069) vs B_fixed 1.244 (gap=-0.066, p=0.2175) vs coach default C 1.134 (gap=+0.043, p=0.3052). MDE at 80% power ~0.180 PPP (SD~0.34).
failure_evidence: Observed gap -0.066 is below MDE 0.180; n=44 cannot distinguish a true null from an effect up to 0.18 PPP.
power_info: n=44; MDE 0.180 PPP at 80% power (SD~0.34); 0.265 if SD~0.5
notes: A is left-skewed (median 1.279 > B_fixed) so MW p=0.2175 for A>B is consistent with a negative mean gap.

title: Adapt vs continue matched-pair overall-offense excess (post-hoc)
hypothesis: Teams that abandon a suppressed play type (h2_n<=1) show a smaller matched-pair overall six-PT H1->H2 excess decline than teams that continue (h2_n>=5).
design: Exploratory, not pre-registered. Group A continue n=11064; Group B adapt n=810 (adapt rate 6.8%). Same-game opponent control, 0.10 H1-PPP caliper, game-cluster-robust SE.
primary_result: Caliper 0.10: A excess +0.076 [+0.068,+0.084] n=3421 p=0; B excess +0.014 [-0.019,+0.046] n=255 p=0.386. Gap B-A = -0.062. Caliper sweep B CIs include 0 except 0.15.
failure_evidence: Group B caliper-0.10 CI includes 0 (p=0.386, n=255 clusters=242); Group B is a reconstructed post-hoc cohort, not a validated successful-adaptation sample.
power_info: B n=255 pairs / 242 games at primary caliper
notes: Not a causal test of pivoting; outcome is six-PT aggregate PPP because suppressed-PT H2 PPP is undefined for abandoners.

title: Dose-response of continuation ratio vs matched excess decline
hypothesis: Among 11064 suppression triggers, higher h2_n/h1_n continuation predicts larger matched-pair excess decline.
design: OLS excess ~ cont_ratio + self_h1 + C(season)+C(play_type), cluster-robust SE by game. Exploratory post-hoc.
primary_result: Raw n=11064: beta_cont=+0.0120, 95% CI [-0.0020,+0.0261], p=0.09336. Caliper 0.10: +0.0095 [-0.0122,+0.0312], p=0.392. All caliper and play-type strata not significant.
failure_evidence: Primary CI includes 0 at n=11064 (p=0.09336); every caliper 0.05-0.30 and all six play types ns.
notes: Pre-specified read was that a CI including zero means no dose-response at this sample size.

title: Adaptation quality vs talent as predictor of series wins
hypothesis: pct_ran_BEST - pct_ran_AVOID predicts series wins after controlling for RS net-rating talent.
design: 110 series-directions / 55 series. Logistic y=won on standardized talent_diff and adapt_diff.
primary_result: corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124. Per-series logistic: talent_diff_z +0.737 p=0.0213; adapt_diff_z +0.328 p=0.2755. Team-in-series cluster: talent p=0.0095, adapt p=0.2449. Univariate adapt beta=+0.311 p=0.1128. LPM: talent +0.160 p=0.0046, adapt +0.072 p=0.2633, R2=0.142.
failure_evidence: After talent control adapt p=0.275; n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.
notes: Authors' honest null: report as confounded with talent.

title: Live Tab-2 trigger timing, 10 series (rest-of-game BEST vs AVOID)
hypothesis: Tab 2's live trigger fires with time to act, and rest-of-game PPP is higher on BEST than AVOID counters.
design: Possession-by-possession replay, 10 2025-26 series. Trigger: H2 PPP drop>=0.25, n>=10 (or n>=5 with eff_n>=300). Counter PPP measured after trigger, not full H2.
primary_result: 101 triggers; 100% actionable (>=5 H2 poss remaining); mean remaining 23.4. Spearman tier vs ROG PPP rho=-0.0457, p=0.45616, n=268. MW BEST 1.227 (n=30) vs AVOID 1.037 (n=95), p=0.073965 (not confirmed at 0.05). Early vs late BEST ROG 1.521 vs 1.182.

notes: Follow-up 25-series replay (APPS-029) confirms BEST vs AVOID.

title: Live Tab-2 trigger timing, 25 series 2025-26
hypothesis: Same live-trigger rest-of-game test on 25 2025-26 playoff series.
design: Same Tab 2 logic as APPS-028; 228 unique triggers; AVOID_OVERRIDE rule added.
primary_result: 228 triggers, 100% actionable, mean remaining 21.0. Spearman rho=-0.2066, p=1e-06, n=557. MW BEST 1.263 (n=57) vs AVOID 0.783 (n=110), p=0.0. Early BEST-AVOID gap 0.701 vs late 0.415.
