title: Coaching alignment: BEST/AVOID run rates vs series wins (55 series)
hypothesis: Teams that run BEST counters more (and AVOID less) after suppression win more series.
design: 633 triggers, 110 series-directions. Spearman of pct triggers ran BEST/AVOID vs series won.
primary_result: % ran BEST 44.7% of triggers / 9.7% volume; % ran AVOID 61.1% / 23.3% volume. Spearman BEST vs won rho=+0.131 p=0.1723; AVOID vs won rho=-0.098 p=0.3099. Mean PPP BEST 1.395 vs AVOID 0.865.
failure_evidence: Alignment-win Spearmans ns (p=0.172 / 0.310) at n=110 directions; INSUFF_EVIDENCE is 91.5% of triggers.
notes: Volume share of BEST is only 9.7%; most H2 counters are INSUFF_EVIDENCE (46.8% volume).

title: Coaching pickup: H1->H2 share shift toward BEST vs AVOID
hypothesis: After suppression, teams shift volume toward the sheet BEST counter and away from AVOID.
design: best_pickup = H2 share - H1 share of BEST counter; 591/633 triggers with BEST defined. Also possession-weighted AVOID vs INSUFF mix H1->H2.
primary_result: % shifted more toward BEST 51.6%; % used more AVOID 22.4%. Avg best pickup +0.0024 pp; BEST share 10.0%->10.2%. PO AVOID share within AVOID+INSUFF 13.4%->13.7% (+0.3 pp); BEST 12.9%->12.8%. RS AVOID +1.1 pp; BEST 13.1%->12.3%.
failure_evidence: BEST pickup +0.24 pp is essentially zero; teams do not shift toward BEST; AVOID ticks up slightly.
notes: INSUFF_EVIDENCE dominates (~83-86% of AVOID+INSUFF possessions).

title: CUT depletion / decay hypothesis (feasibility, not efficiency)
hypothesis: CUT PPP decays across successive H2 runs, so the playsheet should rotate off CUT to SPOT_UP.
design: 311 playoff games, 12361 H2 CUT/SPOT_UP/DRIVE possessions. Decay curve, switch-point vs SPOT_UP, depletion-adjusted Spearman, DP policy vs static.
primary_result: CUT PPP stable 1.60-1.71 for runs 1-5 (all n>=14); runs 6+ n=4/2/0. 62.0% of team-halves never crossed below SPOT_UP (n=405). Depletion-adjusted rho -0.0415 vs baseline -0.2737 (degraded 0.2322). DP -6.7 pts/100 vs static ? invalidated.
failure_evidence: No efficiency cliff; constraint is opportunity (~3-5 CUT per half). DP was built on fabricated decay.
notes: Actionable output was constrained mix tables replacing single-label BEST:CUT.

title: INSUFF_EVIDENCE deep audit (post-orphan-fix)
hypothesis: INSUFF_EVIDENCE counter rows are recoverable missed tree branches rather than true no-history pairs.
design: 1153 counter obs; 427 INSUFF (37.0%). Cause A wrong-src vs Cause B counter-absent. Cap/lift/per-src diagnostics.
primary_result: CAUSE_A n=208 (48.7%, mean PPP 1.162); CAUSE_B n=219 (51.3%, mean 1.055). BEST-AVOID gap 0.620; MISSED_GOOD 1.148 vs AVOID 0.821 (+0.327). Expanding cap 25->50 recovers <=0 confirmed truncated pairs; ADAPT_LIFT_MIN filter 0 rows.
failure_evidence: Audit of coverage, not an outcome test; 37% of counters still unranked.
notes: Highest-ROI model change identified as per-src_pt ranking (recover 208/427) with no new data.

title: Oracle player-routing sensitivity (RS holdout)
hypothesis: Routing regret (+0.137 baseline) is not an artifact of low-volume bench oracles.
design: RS holdout BEST rows n>=5 (980). Ablate min_n gate and top-K rotation filter.
primary_result: Baseline min_n=3: regret +0.137, 63.0% oracle>actual, n=980. min_n=20: +0.050, 52.5%, n=703. Recommended top-8 + min_n=5: +0.094, 57.9%, n=970. Strict top-4+n5: +0.068, 54.8%.
failure_evidence: Regret shrinks under stricter gates but stays positive; recommended cite is +0.094 not +0.137.
notes: Shrinkage prior weight=50 means n=3 H2H is ~94% league mean. PO oracle player tables flagged exploratory (typical n=3-8).

title: Clutch-after-suppression star PPP vs overall (30 stars, RS 2025-26)
hypothesis: Stars elevate in clutch possessions of games where their team had a suppression trigger.
design: Clutch=Q4 last 5 min |margin|<=5. Group X=clutch in suppression games vs Z=overall. n_X>=15; n=24 OK-confidence players. Also raw clutch vs overall table.
primary_result: Mean X-Z uplift -0.065, t=-2.41, p=0.025, n=24 (16 negative / 8 positive). Pearson r(uplift, IE%)=0.031, p=0.885. Brunson X-Z=+0.003 (rank 8/24). Raw clutch vs overall: Edwards +0.225, Giannis -0.240; Brunson -0.021.
failure_evidence: Significant league-wide decline (-0.065 PPP, p=0.025), opposite of elevated clutch-cooking; IE% does not predict uplift.
power_info: n=24 players with n_X>=15; PO replication not run
notes: Selection likely: these clutch minutes occur in games where the offense already failed to adapt.

title: Player-level BEST vs AVOID PPP gap (initiators, 55-series)
hypothesis: The team-level BEST vs AVOID gap holds when H2 possessions are filtered to initiating player.
design: trigger_table_clean.csv; gate n>=10 per tier to report. League aggregate players with n>=15 each tier.
primary_result: Mean gap (n>=10 each tier) +0.427 PPP. Mean BEST 1.347 (38 players) vs AVOID 0.920 (94 players). Stars mean gap +0.542 (n=15) vs role +0.428 (n=16). Only 3 players clear n>=30 both tiers (all BOS: White +0.864, Brown +0.466, Tatum +0.391).
failure_evidence: Pooled player gap +0.427 in the same direction as the team gap; most star cells are below the n>=30 gate.
power_info: 38/94 players at n>=15; only 3 at n>=30 both tiers
notes: Player samples are thin; Brunson BEST n=8 below gate. Related to APPS-015 tendency tables but this is PPP gap not mix share.

title: Sequential possession premium: defensive aftershock by play type
hypothesis: Opponent next-possession PPP is suppressed (positive aftershock) after the offense runs play type X, and this replicates RS+PO vs playoffs.
design: All games H2 sequential pairs. Own-next baseline 0.975 PPP (n=18943); opponent-next baseline 1.206 (n=458604). Aftershock = opp baseline - opp next PPP after X succeeds.
primary_result: All-games aftershock after success: CUT +0.119 (n=21398), DRIVE +0.123 (57621), PNR +0.127 (51194), POST_UP +0.128 (20619), PULL_UP +0.132 (26060), PUTBACK +0.130 (5888), SPOT_UP +0.128 (43857), TRANSITION +0.135 (26262). All 8 replicate in playoffs. Own-next A1 treated as exploratory (~4% of pairs).
failure_evidence: Large-n aftershock is uniformly positive across PTs (opponent scores ~1.07-1.09 vs baseline 1.206) so it may be a generic dead-ball/score effect rather than PT-specific disruption.
notes: Sign convention here (positive aftershock = opponent scores LESS) is opposite of the 52-series net-swing table where DRIVE/POST_UP have negative net swing.

title: Player sequential-premium family (same-player X->Y after opponent response)
hypothesis: Specific player X->Y sequences score above that player's unconditional Y baseline.
design: Same initiator on t and t+2; min n=30; focus pairs CUT->DRIVE, DRIVE->SPOT_UP, etc. Flag |t|>=2.0.
primary_result: Top: P. George DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.560 (n=31, t=+2.2). D. Mitchell SPOT_UP->DRIVE +0.279 (n=56, t=+2.8). Bottom: C. White DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.466 (n=37); D. Bane DRIVE->PNR -0.324 (n=70, t=-2.7). Most cells DIRECTIONAL (n<50).
failure_evidence: Many |t|<2 and n<50; no multiplicity correction; mixed signs on the same pair across players.
notes: Later Brown->Tatum +0.326 (n=43) was shown to be a placebo artifact (APPS-070).

title: Season adapter profiles (BEST-share consistency across seasons)
hypothesis: Teams' post-trigger BEST vs AVOID mix is a stable coaching signature across seasons.
design: BEST share of H2 counter possessions; teams with n>=2 seasons. Consistency=stdev of BEST share.
primary_result: Top mean BEST share: BOS 15.7% (10 dirs, win 70%), LAL 15.5%, GSW 13.8%. Bottom: HOU 2.5%, MIL 3.5%, LAC 4.1%. DEN 4.9% BEST / 70.8% INSUFF yet 62% win. ORL AVOID share 59.3%, 0% win.
failure_evidence: No inferential test of stability vs noise; win% not identified with BEST share (IND 4.5% BEST, 71% win).

title: PUTBACK suppression matched-pair isolation (star vs team)
hypothesis: Conceding a PUTBACK causally suppresses the next offensive possession after matching on game state.
design: PSM 1:3 ATT, caliper 0.05. Treated=just conceded PUTBACK. Covariates include off_margin (already reflects conceded points).
primary_result: TEAM ATT=-0.0038 CI[-0.025,+0.015] perm p=0.890 n_t=15614. STAR ATT=+0.0040 [-0.049,+0.052] p=0.834 n_t=2481. STAR Q4 ATT=-0.1045 [-0.217,+0.010] p=0.032 (gradient does not survive matching as a FINDING).
failure_evidence: Raw putback suppression collapses once margin/state is matched; original finding was a score/context confound.
notes: Knowable: margin already includes the putback points, so unmatched H2/Q4 comparisons confound scoreboard state with aftershock.

title: POST_UP vs PUTBACK Q1-Q4 gradient and double-suppression stack
hypothesis: PUTBACK suppression is fatigue (Q4-heavy); POST_UP is immediate rhythm disruption; stacking them is additive.
design: POST_UP cluster (Jokic, Doncic, LeBron, Fox, Brown) Q1-Q4 deltas; TRANSITION cluster (Tatum, Morant, Young, Haliburton); league POST_UP then PUTBACK 4-hop stack n=1047.
primary_result: POST_UP Q1->Q4 -0.065 (Q1 -0.119 to Q4 -0.184); PUTBACK -0.374 (0.144 to -0.23). TRANSITION cluster gradient +0.075 (unexpected vs hypothesized flat). Stacked delta -0.071 vs additive prediction -0.232 (less than additive). League after PUTBACK -0.113 (n=15898), after POST_UP -0.119 (n=76329).
failure_evidence: PUTBACK vs POST_UP gradients differ as hypothesized, but TRANSITION gradient has the wrong sign and stacked suppression is less than additive; per-player stacked n often <5.
power_info: cluster n=5 players; stacked n=1047 league / typically n<10 per star
notes: Authors read POST_UP as rhythm/read disruption not fatigue; TRANSITION unexpected +0.075 flagged to re-examine sample.

title: PNR suppression RTM-excess team and player tables
hypothesis: PNR H1->H2 drops contain a team- and player-specific RTM-excess signal (who loses PNR; who takes it away).
design: 2838 PNR triggers; matched pairs caliper 0.10 n=380. CR1 cluster SE on game. Player tables also c=0.15/0.20.
primary_result: Offense excess c=0.10: GSW +0.702 n=12; MIA +0.110 CI[-0.119,+0.340] n=15. Defense: DAL +0.761 n=6 (CI crosses 0); UTA -0.005 CI[-0.203,+0.194] n=7. Players c=0.10 n>=5: J. Brown +0.643 n=10; only 2 players n>=10 at this caliper.
failure_evidence: Overlapping CIs; player n>=10 at primary caliper is 2; many team CIs include 0. Ranks not distinguishable.
power_info: 380 matched pairs at c=0.10 from 2838 triggers
notes: CHA/SAC digs are case studies on the same PNR-excess tables, not separate tests.

title: Clutch sequence-premium family (multiple windows)
hypothesis: Star X->Y offensive sequences in clutch have stable premiums across last-5 / last-10 windows.
design: Analysis A: team X then opp then star Y; premium vs star clutch baseline on Y. Windows last 5 min n>=25/30 and last 10 min n>=20/30. Analysis D is opp-suppression, separate.
primary_result: Last 5 n>=25: 18 pos / 11 neg of 29 cells; top S. Curry DRIVE->PULL_UP +0.426 n=28. Last 10 n>=30: 25 pos / 13 neg of 38; top A. Edwards PULL_UP->DRIVE +0.365 n=33. Headline #1 sequence is not stable across windows. No-floor table is dominated by n=1 cells.
failure_evidence: Top cell changes with window/floor; many n~25-35; no pooled test or multiplicity correction.
power_info: 29 cells last5 n>=25; 38 cells last10 n>=30
notes: Family of window variants; conclusions do not stabilize so recorded as one descriptive family rather than separate supported findings.

title: 52-series sequential adaptation: durable pivot branches and net swing
hypothesis: If-X-fails-then-Y pivot branches and PT net-swing (own PPP - opp next PPP) are durable across ~104 playoff team-offense units.
design: 52 series, 104 units. Durable branch: median lift>0 and lift>0 in >=70% of units. Net swing per PT per unit.
primary_result: durable_branches=[]. Median net swing: CUT +0.36 (neg in 9%), TRANSITION +0.26 (21%), PULL_UP +0.09 (33%), PNR +0.04 (45%), SPOT_UP +0.02 (40%), POST_UP -0.22 (77%), DRIVE -0.27 (88%). n_units: CUT 103, DRIVE/POST_UP/SPOT_UP/TRANSITION/PULL_UP 104, PUTBACK 47.
failure_evidence: No conditional pivot branch met the durability bar (empty durable_branches). DRIVE/POST_UP negative net swing is the durable aftershock finding, recorded here as the positive half of the same run.
notes: Verdict is for the pre-specified durable-branch test (null). The aftershock ranking of DRIVE/POST_UP is supported and used as the prior in the net-swing scorer.

title: A1 within-scheme adapter vs wrong-way (selection-controlled)
hypothesis: Within inferred scheme, teams that shift toward SHOULD counters (adapters) have higher early->late dPPP than wrong-way teams, after removing early-PPP selection.
design: Playoff possessions. Within-scheme adapter vs wrong-way; also early-PPP quintile match. Carryover Game N->N+1.
primary_result: DROP: adapt +0.0041 vs wrong -0.0789, gap +0.0830, Welch p=0.0046, n=73/109. HELP: +0.0943 vs +0.0404, gap +0.0539, p=0.0493, n=96/115. SWITCH: +0.1200 vs +0.1399, gap -0.0199, p=0.6514, n=36/50. Pooled quintiles: adapt +0.0667 n=205 vs wrong +0.0111 n=274, gap +0.0556. Carryover next-game PPP gaps ns (DROP +0.0039 p=0.4244).
failure_evidence: DROP/HELP within-scheme gaps are positive; SWITCH has the wrong sign; next-game carryover is null. Early-PPP of wrong_way (1.0939) still exceeds adapters (1.0448).
notes: Wrote to fix unfair T1 that compared adapters to no_signal cells that never started hot.

title: Historical series_analysis backtest: winner and PT-rank Spearman
hypothesis: Pregame predicted series winner and predicted PT-PPP ranks match realized playoff series outcomes.
design: 45 series_analysis.md reports (51 slug folders). Winner from predictions.json vs actual. Spearman of pregame PT PPP ranks vs observed series PPP-by-PT. Canonical-10 Spearmans tabulated in Chat 6.
primary_result: Winner: 27 CONFIRMED / 18 CONTRADICTED of 45 (60%). Canonical-10 team-side Spearman median ~0.536 (20 sides); series-mean median ~0.554. Example phi_bos_2526: predicted BOS (85.2% conf, PHI baseline 7.4%) CONTRADICTED (PHI 4-3); scheme-adjusted Spearman PHI 0.714, BOS 0.452. Chat 6 also cites RS holdout methodology rho=0.54, n=454, MAE 0.0922 PPP from pipeline_report_metadata.json.
failure_evidence: Winner hit 27/45 with no CI; per-series Spearmans range from PHI_BKN -0.024 to MIN_DEN 0.905; RS 0.54 is a hand-maintained headline file.
power_info: 45 series with series_analysis.md; canonical 10 for tabulated rho
notes: Family of repeated series backtests. Individual TEAM_vs_TEAM generated reports in reports/ and demo_reports/ were not scored as experiments. Remaining 6 series_analysis folders lack series_analysis.md.

title: SQ2 holdout protocol specified but not scored
hypothesis: A frozen-engine hit rate on 25 holdout series (cap_yy>23) is the defensible SQ2 number, vs in-sample 69.8%.
design: Engine SHA freeze 59a9be48; tuning 17 series cap_yy<=23; holdout 25 series. Protocol written; holdout scoring result not found in files read.
primary_result: No holdout hit-rate number found. Protocol states existing --full-calibrated 69.8% is in-sample until the holdout is run.
failure_evidence: Holdout was specified (SHA 59a9be48, 17/25 split) but no scored holdout output was located in this slice.
notes: Confirms APPS-003 note that the holdout protocol exists without a result file.

title: Observed on-ball defensive scheme labels (ORL-DET G1)
hypothesis: NBA matchup/PBP fields can label on-ball coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) at usable rates.
design: Single game 0042500101. Confident labels vs OTHER.
primary_result: DET: 67 on-ball HC poss, 10 labeled (14.9%) ? DROP n=5 PPP=1.20, ICE_CANDIDATE n=5 PPP=0.80, OTHER n=57 PPP=1.42. ORL: 60 poss, 2 labeled (3.3%). switches_on unpopulated.
failure_evidence: Confident label rates 14.9% and 3.3%; NBA matchups feed did not populate switches_on.
notes: ICE_CANDIDATE is unconfirmed without screen-contact tracking.

title: Sequence-memory horizon test (per-lag vs aggregated window)
hypothesis: Increasing prior-possession history changes the opponent's next-possession outcome after controlling for game state.
design: 1024980 possessions with >=8 priors; TRAIN 22-24, VAL 24-25, TEST 2025-26. Per-lag vs aggregated window; GBT/logit/ridge.
primary_result: Per-lag GBT AUC N=0 0.5621 -> N=1 0.5863 (d+0.0242) -> N=3 0.5907 -> N=8 0.5911. R2 0.0051 -> 0.0133. Aggregated window declines after N=1 (AUC 0.5868 -> 0.5687 at N=8). Effective horizon ~2-3 possessions.
failure_evidence: Short-memory horizon is stable OOS; almost all gain is lag-1, plateau by lag 4. Absolute AUC still only ~0.591.
notes: Aggregated-window decline was dilution of lag-1, not absence of memory.

title: Test 1: 8x8 action transition matched ATT matrix
hypothesis: Predecessor play type A changes PPP of next play type B after exact matching, surviving BH-FDR and placebo.
design: 64 A->B cells. Exact match margin_bucket x period x season x offensive team. Cluster bootstrap 1000; perm 2000; placebo 1000; BH across 64. Min n=30.
primary_result: 1 of 64 survived matching+BH+placebo: CUT->PNR ATT=-0.0502*. Top unsigned ATT PUTBACK->PUTBACK +0.0615 CI[-0.060,+0.168] not sig. TRANSITION->DRIVE +0.0355 perm_p=0.0020 BH_adj_p=0.0640.
failure_evidence: Pre-registered bar: 1/64 cells survived; no structural coaching prescription from isolated cells.
notes: Directional row means: T=TRANSITION 6/8 next-pairs positive (mean ATT +0.0141); T+1=PNR 1/8 preceding positive.

title: Test 2: PUTBACK Q4 star-suppression IVW trend
hypothesis: Star PPP after conceding a putback declines monotonically Q1->Q4.
design: Matched ATT by quarter; IVW trend; quarter-shuffle placebo 5000x; Cochran-Armitage P(score). Treated=2481, control capped 60000.
failure_evidence: Trend clears IVW, placebo, and Q4 CI excludes 0 in RS/close. Mechanism unresolved (Test 3 null) and playoff subset underpowered.
notes: Console verdict said WEAK SIGNAL; header said FINDING (qualified). Recorded as supported-with-qualifications; Test 3 shows load is not the mechanism.

title: Test 3: cumulative Q1-Q3 star load -> Q4 PPP
hypothesis: High Q1-Q3 initiator load lowers Q4 star PPP (mechanism for Test 2).
design: Unit=(star, game). Top vs bottom tercile Q1-Q3 load; match Q4 margin x opp def-rating quartile x season x home.
primary_result: Matched ATT=-0.0052, 95% CI[-0.0387,+0.0239], perm p=0.7706, placebo p=0.7760. Raw high-low -0.0146. high-load games=1854, low=2375.
failure_evidence: ATT~0, CI excludes large load effects; perm/placebo ~0.77. Test 2 Q4 decline is not explained by raw possession load.

title: Test 4: foul-trouble sequencing after star 2nd Q1/Q2 foul
hypothesis: Opponent PPP rises on the next 1-3 possessions after a star's 2nd personal foul in Q1/Q2.
design: 2104 qualifying events. Exact match period x margin x season x offensive team. FT possessions excluded after first-pass artifact.
primary_result: Including FT: lag-1 ATT=+0.204 CI[+0.163,+0.245] (artifact: FT share 41.8% vs 9.9%). Excluding FT: lag-1 +0.0486 [-0.0060,+0.0991] perm p=0.0655; lag-2 -0.0192; lag-3 -0.0272. No lag clears CI+perm+placebo.
failure_evidence: Headline +0.204 was FT-possession coding; clean lag-1 +0.049 does not clear the pre-specified bars.
notes: Knowable: a 2nd foul is often a shooting foul, so lag-1 includes FT trips unless excluded. On-floor vs benched not verifiable.

title: Gate 1: defensive assignment network modularity vs volume-schedule null
hypothesis: Attacker-defender assignment networks have community structure beyond volume and schedule.
design: 2023-24 RS. attackers=257 defenders=252 possessions=196782. Compare Q_obs to Q_null.
primary_result: Q_obs=0.3838; Q_null=0.4300+-0.0010 range[0.4282,0.4324]; z=-46.85 p_emp=1.000. VERDICT: KILL ? no structure beyond volume+schedule.
failure_evidence: Observed modularity is below the volume-schedule null (z=-46.85); gate instruction is do NOT lean on topology.
notes: gate2_reassignment_probe.py exists but no saved result file was found in sequence_memory/output.

title: Brown-initiated possession -> Tatum next-possession ATT
hypothesis: A Jaylen Brown-initiated BOS possession raises Tatum's points on the next BOS possession (spillover/gravity).
design: Chain N=6992; treated=1173 control=5819. PSM 1:3 caliper 0.05; exact-match fallback; perm 800; placebo 200.
primary_result: PSM ATT=-0.0165, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0924,+0.0605]. Exact-match ATT=-0.0857. Stratified perm p=0.0275 on ATT=-0.0171. Placebo 95% [-0.0762,+0.0730]; real ATT inside. Playoffs ATT=+0.0485 CI[-0.1095,+0.2078].
failure_evidence: PSM CI includes 0; ATT inside placebo range; not robustly >0. Perm p=0.0275 is on a near-zero negative ATT.
notes: Verdict: NO ROBUST EFFECT, consistent with spillover/state-transition artifact.

title: Brown DRIVE -> Tatum PNR sequential-premium placebo
hypothesis: The reported +0.326 Brown->Tatum PNR premium is Brown-specific, not any-teammate DRIVE->Tatum PNR.
design: 99 BOS DRIVE->Tatum-PNR chains (Brown 43 / other 56). Placebo 5000 relabels; also league-wide teammate-DRIVE->PNR.
primary_result: Reproduced premium +0.3262 n=43 vs Tatum PNR baseline 1.0459. Brown-other gap +0.3185, MW p=0.1702. Placebo 95% [-0.1389,+0.4192], observed inside, p=0.1136; perm p=0.2034. League teammate-DRIVE->PNR controlled beta=+0.0220 p=0.0044 n_t=20658 (tiny). Tatum any-teammate +0.1524 p=0.2546, perm inside.
failure_evidence: Brown-specific +0.326 does not survive placebo; any teammate's DRIVE produces a comparable number. League effect is +0.02 PPP.
notes: Knowable: original n=43, t=+1.7 was already below |t|=2.

title: Opponent action T -> your offense T+1 (def-matched 8x8)
hypothesis: The opponent's previous play type changes your next-possession PPP after matching on defensive team.
design: 64 cells; def_tri matching primary; sensitivity match on own offense. BH-FDR+placebo+FT-clean. prev_made control.
primary_result: 3/64 FINDING cells survive both matchings: SPOT_UP->TRANSITION ATT=-0.085; POST_UP->TRANSITION -0.083; PNR->DRIVE -0.058 (all also survive +prev_made). PULL_UP->DRIVE dropped as defense-quality confound.
failure_evidence: Three cells replicate under def-match, off-match, and prev_made control. Most of 64 are null.
notes: Weight row-level patterns over single cells per the report. Offensive-team match is the sensitivity file.

title: Possession Control Index incremental R2 over ORtg (PCI is DRtg proxy)
hypothesis: PCI (halfcourt PPP + second-chance - TO - transition leakage) explains Net Rating beyond ORtg, Pace, and FGA/poss.
design: 120 team-seasons. Models A baseline / B PCI-only / C full. OOS test 2025-26. Diagnostic Net~ORtg+leakage vs +offcontrol.
primary_result: A R2=0.763 OOS 0.761; C R2=0.902 OOS 0.919; dR2=+0.139. Offensive-control components add +0.005 R2 beyond ORtg. Net~ORtg+leakage R2=0.948. corr(leakage, DRtg)=+0.894. PCI univariate r=+0.863 vs ORtg +0.866.
failure_evidence: Headline PCI gain is leakage tracking DRtg (+0.89); offensive-control dR2=+0.005. Baseline omitted defense by construction (Net=ORtg-DRtg).
notes: Knowable: Net Rating already contains DRtg, so adding a leakage term that correlates 0.89 with DRtg must lift R2.

title: State persistence vs window-overlap null (pre-registered FAIL)
hypothesis: Process-only latent state (PCA-1 of tempo/transition) persists above the rolling-window overlap null after game x team demeaning.
design: N=1060893 possessions, 4 seasons, W=3 lagged. Excess = observed r - window-overlap null. Pre-registered criterion: excess persistence.
primary_result: Process-only lag-1 r=+0.645 vs null +0.655; EXCESS=-0.010, cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [-0.012,-0.009]. Scoring excess -0.000; action texture +0.003. Instantaneous scoring autocorr lag-1=-0.0128.
failure_evidence: HEADLINE FAIL: excess=-0.010 with CI entirely negative; state persistence does not clear the overlap null. No state-persistence paper.
notes: High raw r~0.65 is mechanical window overlap. Season-stable observed r 0.642-0.647.

title: H1 usage as predictor of H2 suppression (distribution shift)
hypothesis: First-half reliance on a play type predicts second-half suppression after controlling for H1 PPP / mean reversion.
design: 8873 team-games, 37067 cells (>=4 poss both halves). Test A slope; Test B matched HIGH vs LOW H1 usage; Test C multinomial which-type-suppressed.
primary_result: Test B: all BH-adjusted null/WEAK (PNR ATT=+0.0313 BH_p=0.0658 WEAK; others NULL). Test C top-1 acc=0.550 vs mean-reversion baseline 0.511 (+0.039) vs most-used 0.239. Test A PULL_UP slope -0.0581 p=0.0030; CUT -0.0917 p=0.0410; PNR +0.0562 p=0.0005 (wrong sign for suppression).
failure_evidence: Matched ATT does not survive BH; predictive lift over mean reversion is only +0.039 (0.550 vs 0.511). Bulk of H2 suppression is RTM.
power_info: n=8873 team-games; Test C test n=1008
notes: Headline: no robust evidence H1 reliance predicts H2 suppression.

title: Memoryless Monte Carlo possession simulation (generative check)
hypothesis: A memoryless state-driven process calibrated to NBA micro-stats can match uncalibrated distributional targets (esp. lag-1 scoring autocorr).
design: 10000 games x 200 possessions. Constraint state_{t+1} indep play_type_t | state_t. Not a validation of empirical findings used as anchors.
primary_result: Uncalibrated: PPP std 1.149 vs sim 1.152; lag-1 scoring autocorr real -0.0022 vs sim +0.0029; share 0 pts 0.475 vs 0.484. Sequence-only R2=0.00000; state-only 0.00002.
failure_evidence: Generative existence proof, not independent evidence. Sequence R2~0 by construction of the constraint.
notes: Status line in the report: GENERATIVE / ILLUSTRATIVE, not validation.

title: MC suppression check: memoryless sim vs Paper 1 DiD +0.408
hypothesis: A memoryless process matching possession micro-stats will reproduce the Paper 1 matched DiD suppression excess.
design: Same 10000x200 sim; H1 steps 0-49 / H2 50-99; trigger h1_ppp>=1.15 and drop; NN match caliper 0.1.
primary_result: Sim DiD ATT=-0.076 [-0.081,-0.071] n_pairs=25561 vs real +0.408; gap +0.484. Trigger count 25564 (32.9% of game x PT cells) vs ~5500 RS. Raw unmatched decline sim -0.504 vs real ~-0.655.
failure_evidence: Sim ATT near 0 (slightly negative) as RTM+matching requires; cannot close the +0.408 real excess. Supports that half-level suppression is not memoryless microdynamics.
notes: Verdict of this check is that the real Paper 1 number is an anomaly vs the sim (near-zero sim ATT). Runtime field '1783832484s' is a clock artifact, not a measured runtime.

title: Persistent Impact Score lag curves (global then within-team)
hypothesis: Running play type X raises the same team's next 1-5 possession PPP vs a matched baseline (action memory).
design: Global baseline then re-center on team-season mean. PNR inferrer-only; OT+garbage excluded; min n>=30.
primary_result: Global horizons: DRIVE/SPOT_UP/TRANSITION=5; others 0 (PNR/CUT/POST_UP/PUTBACK). SPOT_UP lag-1 lift +0.027 ctrl_p=0.0000. Within-team: all horizons 0 except SPOT_UP horizon(all)=1; PNR lag-1 within_team_lift=-0.0218.

title: Gravity persistence: elite creator -> teammate PPP at lags 1-3
hypothesis: After an elite creator's signature action, teammates score more on the team's next k possessions with the same lineup on the floor.
design: Exact match offensive lineup_id x margin bucket x period. 8 creators x 3 lags. BH-FDR 24 PPP cells.
primary_result: All 8 creators horizon=0. Jokic lag-1 ATT=+0.0282 CI[-0.043,+0.099] p=0.3779. CLEAN NULL on teammate PPP. Secondary: Antetokounmpo +0.075 distinct initiators over next 3 poss (perm p=0.0002, BH 0.003) ? structure not efficiency.
failure_evidence: No elite creator produces a positive lineup-matched teammate-PPP lift at any lag.
power_info: Jokic lag-1 n=1880; Giannis n=1804; Doncic n=325
notes: Usage redistribution without points payoff for Giannis is the only surviving structural cell.

title: Extended Possession Value (direct PPP + opponent T+1 suppression)
hypothesis: Play types and players have a real downstream (opponent next-PPP) component beyond direct PPP.
design: Exact match margin x period x season x focal team. Ext.Value = direct PPP + (-opp ATT). BH+placebo for downstream.
primary_result: 4/8 PTs downstream real: CUT Ext 1.658 (supp +0.0220), TRANSITION 1.509 (+0.0145), SPOT_UP 1.303 (+0.0124), POST_UP 1.127 (+0.0194). DRIVE downstream not real (opp ATT +0.0024). Player downstream mostly BH ns except M. McBride supp +0.1007 BH p=0.0000.
failure_evidence: Downstream effects are small (~0.01-0.02 PPP) relative to direct PPP gaps; player list is mostly non-FINDING after BH.
power_info: PT-level n in the tens to hundreds of thousands implied by other seq files
notes: POST_UP has low direct PPP (1.107) but real downstream suppression, opposite of the 52-series negative net-swing ranking which uses own-PPP minus opp-next without this matching.

title: Trigger attribution: variance of H1->H2 PPP collapse
hypothesis: Observable in-game process/usage/shot-selection/lineup/context changes explain suppression triggers beyond RTM.
design: 40963 team-game-PT rows (>=5 both halves), 5234 games. Nested OLS on ppp_change. Triggers 12617 (30.8%), mean collapse -0.612.
primary_result: RTM (ppp_h1 alone) 32.9% of variance. Usage +0.0%; process+shot-zone +1.7%; lineup +0.0%; context +0.0%. Unexplained 65.4%. Total explained 34.6% (RTM=95% of explained).
failure_evidence: Process/usage/lineup/context add ~1.7 pp; residual 65.4% is idiosyncratic noise from small per-half n.
notes: Consistent with distribution-shift null: collapses are mostly hot first halves cooling off.

title: Star-specific 8x8 transition matrices (30 stars)
hypothesis: Teammate DRIVE -> star PNR (inferrer-only) is a recurring setup; other star transitions are structural if they FIND in 3+ stars.

primary_result: Pre-reg DRIVE->PNR: all NULL/WEAK (SGA ATT=-0.222 BH_p=0.433). FINDING cells: 2 (Curry CUT->DRIVE +0.460 n=66 LOW_CONFIDENCE; Leonard SPOT_UP->POST_UP -0.360 n=137). Zero transition types FIND in 3+ stars. WEAK: 36.
failure_evidence: Pre-registered hypothesis untestable (insufficient inferrer-only n) and unreplicated; 2 isolated FINDING cells expected at ~5% of 883 tests.

title: Channel 2: possession ending state vs next 90-180s volume/points
hypothesis: A possession's ending state changes opponent points/possessions in the next 90-180s beyond ~0.01-0.02 PPP boundary drift.
design: 911968 possessions. Baseline end state MADE_DEAD. Same-period clock windows.
primary_result: 90s vs MADE_DEAD: TURNOVER_LIVE dOppPts=+0.510 dNetPts=-0.306 (dOppPPP=+0.055, dOppPoss=+0.298); MISSED_DEAD dNetPts=-0.112; PUTBACK dNetPts=+0.078. Volume (dOppPoss), not PPP, carries most of the live-TO cost.

title: State-attribution AUC decomposition of lag-1 memory
hypothesis: Lag-1 predictive signal is process/state (pace, play type, transition) rather than outcome persistence.

primary_result: Total attributable +0.0614 AUC. outcome_persistence marginal +0.0527 (39% share) unique +0.0069; momentum +0.0494 unique 0; transition_state unique +0.0117 (53% of unique); playtype_state unique +0.0003; lineup_state unique -0.0049.

power_info: 2025-26 test set; original N0->N1 jump +0.0242 for reference
notes: Collinear blocks: momentum large alone, unique 0.

title: Paper 2 topological-identity gate and confirmatory (P1a/P1b)

hypothesis: Offenses have identifiable structural hubs (F1a usage-decoupled; F1b load correlates with fragility) at full scale.

title: Portability confirmatory: wiring-displacement signature travels
hypothesis: A player's wiring-displacement signature is a portable trait (self_sim > decoy_sim at destination).

primary_result: median self_sim=+0.129 decoy_sim=+0.049; T1 median Delta=+0.0557 perm_p=0.0050; 173/294=0.5884 sign_test_p=2.872e-03; dest-fr CI [+0.0192,+0.0859]. All three decision-rule bars True. T1 CONFIRMED.

title: Connector teammate-path quality Q_p split-half reliability
hypothesis: Connector quality Q_p (teammate-initiated on-off PPP gap) is a stable player-season attribute.
design: Odd/even game_id split; n=102 connectors with both halves; on&off >=80 poss/half, teammate-init on >=50. Spearman-Brown; ANOVA ICC.
primary_result: Pearson r(Q_a,Q_b)=+0.215 p=0.0297; Spearman rho=+0.242. Spearman-Brown Q~0.355, S~0.278. Sign agreement 65.7% (67/102) binomial p=0.000996. ICC(player-season)=0.216 (78.4% within). Attenuation: even a perfect predictor max |r| with Q_p ~0.595; true r=0.30 attenuates to 0.179 (often undetectable).
failure_evidence: Split-half r=0.215 / SB 0.355 is too low to treat Q_p as a stable scoutable trait; most variance is within-player half-to-half.
notes: L(p)/shape nulls are not just attenuation of a large true effect (true r<=0.25 could still be missed).

title: Connector ecosystem quality: L(p) and |dA| do not predict Q_p
hypothesis: Scalar structural load L(p) or an |dA|-weighted ecosystem lift predicts teammate-path quality Q_p.
design: N=102 connectors (pos=53, neg=49). Talent+opp+period+score residualized S_p and Q_p.
primary_result: L(p) vs Q_p r~0. Uniform mean tm_dPPP vs Q_p r=+0.812; |dA|-weighted eco r=+0.703; eco residualized on uniform vs Q_p r=+0.084 p=0.399 NULL. Cosine to mean positive footprint vs Q_p r=-0.336 p=0.000559 (wrong sign). Pair-level dA contrasts do not survive FDR.
failure_evidence: Proposed structural metrics add nothing beyond a uniform average of teammate lifts (eco residual r=+0.084 p=0.399). Load is not quality.
notes: Together with portability: signature may travel but connector *value* looks relational/context-specific.

title: Connector tangible impact: star shielding, TO, lineup lift
hypothesis: Connector presence shields stars (higher TS, lower TO) and lifts lineup ORtg beyond talent.
design: 61 star-season pairs >=80 poss w/wo CONNECTOR. HasConn M1 regressions. Lineup lift talent-controlled and held-4 swap n=296. Wilcoxon battery n=73.
primary_result: Star dTS +0.05 pp p=0.937; dTO +0.74 pp p=0.00364 (wrong sign for shielding). Star-init TO~HasConn beta=+0.34 pp p=0.439. HasConn on-off PPP BOTH_NULL (mean -0.041 p=0.939, median +0.528 p=0.731, n=73). Frequent-conn lineup ORtg lift LOO +1.559 p=0.0184 but talent-controlled beta +0.915 p=0.51 n=428. Held-4 swap dORtg +0.427 p=0.565 n=296.
failure_evidence: PPP/TS/eFG shielding null; TO rate rises with connectors. Lineup ORtg lift is a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT; swap p=0.565).
power_info: n=61 star pairs; 73 team-seasons; 296 held-4 swaps; 428 lineups
notes: Wilcoxon agrees with means on the nulls (BOTH_NULL) and on TO (BOTH_SIG, higher TO with HasConn).

title: Offensive-identity resilience: connector absence vs usage-matched others
hypothesis: Connector absence displaces team offensive identity (D_A) more than usage-matched non-organizer absence.
design: Player-seasons >=400 poss on and off, N=908. Primary: usage-matched pairs connector vs role occupant / vs terminal.
primary_result: Unmatched conn vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97 p=2.87e-08. Usage-matched vs role: paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35 p=7.35e-09 n=96. Vs terminal: +0.0777 t=2.37 p=0.0261 n=25.
failure_evidence: Usage-matched connector vs role occupant identity break is large and significant (n=96). Licensed comparison excludes organizers.
power_info: n=96 matched pairs vs role; n=25 vs terminal; 908 player-seasons
notes: Does not claim PPP value. PRIMARY ORGANIZER is a positive-control reference (mean D_A 0.2141).

title: Connector on/off scoring vs structural load L (quadrants)
hypothesis: Higher structural load L predicts higher adjusted on-off scoring among connectors.
design: 102 connectors, >=150 on and off. Adj = within-team-season association with opp/period/margin/TALENT. Quadrants at median L=0.037 and median adj=0.10.
primary_result: Corr(L, raw)=+0.013; Corr(L, adj)=+0.008. Quadrants ~25 each of highL-highScore / highL-lowScore / lowL-highScore / lowL-lowScore. Negative on/off n=49; 78% mechanism NONINITIATOR_TEAM_PATH (noninit_team_lift -3.52 vs +2.44 for positives).
failure_evidence: L is uncorrelated with scoring impact (r=+0.008). High-L connectors split evenly into help and harm.
notes: Negative-connector harm is mostly teammate-path efficiency, not mix or initiator replacement.

title: Connector diet x destination structural-gap match
hypothesis: Diet-matching to a destination's thin initiation jobs predicts better post-move outcomes than mismatch.
design: 198 movers with complete diet+gap; taxonomy CONNECTOR n=19; travel-check n=40. match_score=cosine(diet, gap). Primary outcomes portability delta / embedded / d_mpg / d_hhi_top, not PPP.

failure_evidence: Connector subsets n=19/40; all-movers binary delta p=0.0283 does not replicate as a continuous Spearman and is not the licensed connector test.
power_info: n=19 taxonomy connectors; n=198 all movers
notes: Knowable: 15.7% match rate leaves n_match=5 in the taxonomy CONNECTOR cell.

title: Cut-share x load 2x2 connector PPP (id-keyed, after collision fix)
hypothesis: High-CUT portable-diet connectors have higher on/off adj PPP, especially when combined with high load.

title: HasConn share vs pace (possessions per 48)
hypothesis: Connector presence slows pace (substituting half-court organization for transition).
design: Period-implied poss/48; n=28569 periods, 90 team-seasons. HasConn share with score-margin/period/opp FE, team-season FE, cluster SE. Play-mix: HasConn>=1 vs 0 within team-season n=73.
primary_result: beta(HasConn share -> poss/48)=-0.86 SE=0.38 t=-2.25 p=0.0266; within-ts corr=-0.002 p=0.782. Mix: TRANSITION -0.448 pp p=0.0013; PNR +0.980 p=0.00187; CUT +1.353 p=1.2e-11; DRIVE -0.542 p=0.0206; SPOT_UP -1.248 p=0.000315. PUTBACK +0.148 p=0.0579. TRANSITION PPP | HasConn adj -0.13 t=-0.06 p=0.948.
failure_evidence: Pace beta p=0.0266 but within-ts correlation is 0; no stint clock so poss/48 is period-implied. Mix shifts are clearer than efficiency.
notes: HasConn->TRANSITION PPP was mix-licensed and null. Association not causal pace.

hypothesis: Successful vs failing connectors share a structural signature, diet-gap match, or roster-load pattern.

primary_result: Pearson r=+0.25 across 30 teams
failure_evidence: r=+0.25; paper: counter-selection quality explains little cross-sectional winning
notes: Descriptive companion to the ladder; NYK 68.8% no-counter / 41% wins vs IND 18.6% BEST follow / 71.4% wins.

title: Full-pool V1: real absences move the fingerprint beyond sampling noise
hypothesis: More than 5% of player-seasons exceed their own null 95th percentile of displacement, and mean excess is positive (V1).
design: 986 eligible player-seasons 2022-25 (30 franchises); rotation subset 478 with mpg>=15 and gp>=30; franchise-clustered inference.
primary_result: all: 16.4% above own p95, binomial p=7.0e-40, mean excess +0.035 CI[+0.029,+0.040]; rotation: 20.5%, p=1.2e-32, excess +0.041 CI[+0.034,+0.047]
failure_evidence: 16.4% vs 5% null; CI on excess excludes 0
notes: Full-season fingerprints include absence-period teammate play. Early n=23 test (PAP-023) was underpowered for V2, not V1.

title: Full-pool V2: structural influence ranks realized displacement
hypothesis: Higher L_pred predicts larger D_real (V2a raw; V2b size-partial).
design: Same 986/478 pool; Spearman; franchise-block 5,000 permutations and cluster bootstrap.
failure_evidence: no franchise shuffle in 5,000 reached the observed statistic
notes: Reverses the n=23 V2 null (PAP-023) with the full pool. Look-ahead remains (PAP-048).

title: Pre-absence L_pre ranks spell displacement (time-ordered)
hypothesis: L computed only from games before an absence spell still ranks D_real.
design: 148 spells, 28 franchises, spell>=15 consecutive absences; L_pre from pre games only; size-partial Spearman; 2,000 franchise bootstrap/perm.
failure_evidence: size-partial +0.353, perm p=0.0005
notes: Design specified after full-pool results. Same seasons as the 986 pool, not an independent replication. Eligibility/case rule fixed before case outcomes.

title: Mechanical floor: L_pre tracks deletion, not teammate change beyond it
hypothesis: The L_pre vs D_real ranking is accounted for by deleting the player's initiations with teammates held fixed, not by teammate reorganization beyond that floor.
design: 148 spells; floor = pre vs pre with row deleted (20 balanced replicates); drift placebo = first vs second half of pre window, player present.
primary_result: L_pre vs floor +0.432 CI[+0.336,+0.528] p=0.0005; L_pre vs D_real-minus-floor +0.082 CI[-0.104,+0.251] p=0.34; L_pre vs drift +0.094 CI[-0.043,+0.218] p=0.30; high-load (n=8) floor share of D_real median 83%; 8/8 high-load above own p95 vs 41% of 140 low-load
failure_evidence: remainder correlation +0.082 CI includes 0; floor correlation +0.432
notes: Added after main pre-absence results. High-load n=8 cannot separate L from usage. CSV: mean D_real 0.152, mean D_mech 0.102, mean D_drift 0.101.

title: Usage, co-absence, and conventional-stat controls on the pre-absence ranking
hypothesis: The ranking is a restatement of usage, simultaneous roster loss, or box-score features.
design: Size-partial Spearman on 148 spells; usage control and top usage tercile; co-absence control; add L_pre to initiation share/usage/minutes/points/on-off for oos displacement.
primary_result: also controlling usage +0.356 CI[+0.214,+0.468]; top usage tercile n=50 +0.521 CI[+0.288,+0.700]; controlling drift +0.345; adding L to conventional stats raised oos accuracy but CI on the improvement includes 0
failure_evidence: usage control leaves +0.356; incremental-value CI includes 0 so L is not shown to beat the box score
notes: Incremental-value result is inconclusive; ranking itself is not usage.

title: Play-type mix is nearly unchanged after an absence
hypothesis: The absent player's departure causes the team to shift which play types it runs overall.
design: Compare team play-type mix pre vs spell on the 148 spells.
primary_result: play-type mix after an absence was nearly identical to the pre-absence mix (paper; no numeric table)
failure_evidence: stated nearly identical; no CI

title: Gate1 G1: fingerprint is invariant to uniform teammate volume scaling
hypothesis: Uniformly scaling remaining teammates' initiation rows by 1.25 leaves the unit fingerprint at Monte Carlo noise (so restoration is not mere volume).
design: 148 spells; cosine distance after x1.25 vs MC redraw of the same matrix.
primary_result: g1_mc median=0.0053 mean=0.0072; g1_scale median=0.0070 mean=0.0090; 95th pct scale=0.0265 from CSV (script also cites sampling-null median ~0.078)
failure_evidence: scaling median 0.007 vs MC noise 0.005
notes: Paper: scaling by 25% moved the fingerprint by essentially game-to-game noise.

title: Gate1 restoration/reorganization placebo (shared-noise construction)
hypothesis: Real-absence restoration R and orthogonal reorganization O exceed a no-absence placebo (same-games construction).
design: 148 spells; R and O from late-pre vs spell vs early-pre vs late-pre with player deleted; franchise bootstrap.
primary_result: CSV: mean R=0.580 vs placebo Rp=0.428 (diff +0.151); mean O=0.462 vs Op=0.406 (diff +0.056); paper: first version showed restoration +0.43 in a placebo with no absence
failure_evidence: placebo restoration +0.43 (paper) / CSV Rp mean +0.428 from shared sampling noise; construction discarded
notes: Outcome measure revised once, before any predictor was examined. Cross-fitted gate2 is the reported estimator.

title: Cross-fitted teammate restoration vs no-absence placebo
hypothesis: Teammates rebuild a detectable fraction of the deleted structural relationships relative to a no-absence placebo.
design: 148 spells; cross-fit deletion direction and counterfactual on random halves of pre games; franchise cluster bootstrap 2,000.
primary_result: restoration mean +0.186 vs placebo +0.013, difference +0.173 [+0.085,+0.262]; 72% of spells R>0 vs 53% placebo; teammate response distance T 0.151 vs 0.139, diff +0.012 [-0.004,+0.030]; equal-size O excess +0.056 [+0.034,+0.080]
failure_evidence: restoration excess +0.173 CI excludes 0; T excess CI includes 0
notes: About one-fifth of deleted structure is restored; four-fifths stays deleted. Average only.

title: Split-half reliability gate on restoration (threshold 0.40)
hypothesis: Per-spell restoration is reliable enough (Spearman-Brown >=0.40) to test predictors of who rebuilds.
design: Independent halves: odd pre+odd spell vs even pre+even spell; 0.40 threshold set before any predictor was examined.
primary_result: SB restoration all spells 0.32; among 53 spells with L_pre>=0.02, SB=0.01 (CSV Spearman +0.004); excess-reorganization upper bound 0.38
failure_evidence: split-half reliability 0.32 < 0.40; 0.01 among L_pre>=0.02
power_info: n=148; 53 with L_pre>=0.02; paper: roughly twice as many spells would be needed
notes: 15-40 game absences over three seasons were known to be short for a 28-cell fingerprint. No predictor was tested.

title: Prespecified predictors of restoration (not evaluated after reliability fail)
hypothesis: Remaining-rotation overlap, presence of a second hub, and uniqueness of the absent player predict restoration.
design: Three predictors specified in advance; none evaluated because PAP-054 failed.
failure_evidence: blocked by restoration reliability 0.32<0.40

title: Pre-absence absorber rules vs realized initiation gainer
hypothesis: The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.
design: Eligible candidates: last-5-games roster with >=100 pre initiations; chance ~1/7.6; 148 spells plus 11 cases.
primary_result: profile match 19% (chance 14%); most minutes 3%; most initiations 5%; same position+minutes 7%; 0/6 high-load cases; 2/11 cases (both low-disruption); minutes-gainer during spell matches initiation gainer 66%
failure_evidence: 19% vs 14% chance; 0/6 hubs; only the during-spell minutes rule works (66%) and is not pre-absence
notes: Best predictor is minutes change during the absence, observed after it starts.

title: Pre-registered case forecasts (11 absences)
hypothesis: High L_pre (>=0.10) forecasts large, pattern-matching reorganization; low L_pre forecasts little change.
design: Selection hashed before stage 2: 3 highest L plus 90/75/50/25/10th percentiles, distinct players, plus 3 supplementary high-load outside July core.
primary_result: 2/6 high-load clean hits (Brunson dir 0.75 [p95 0.49]; Davis 0.88 [0.37]); Booker pattern right magnitude smaller (0.87); Wembanyama magnitude right pattern wrong (0.29 [0.38]); Poeltl and Maxey confounded (co-abs 0.52/0.41); 4/5 low-load accurate; Langford non-specific; descriptive Spearman L vs excess +0.79 (11) / +0.71 (8)
failure_evidence: only 2 of 6 high-load cases clean on both magnitude and pattern; n=8 high-load in pool
notes: Stratified cases are descriptive, not a test. Pool statistic is PAP-047. n_runs counts the 11 forecasts.

title: Structural disruption vs points per possession
hypothesis: How much the offense reorganizes (relative to L) predicts the change in points per possession.
design: 986 player-seasons (paper); scouting S3: 148 spells, partial Spearman of L_pre with Delta PPP controlling conventional features, opponent, home, rest.
primary_result: paper: essentially no relationship on 986; S3 PPP rho=-0.040 CI[-0.212,+0.166] p=0.62; TO +0.033 p=0.70; FT rate +0.161 p=0.061; robustness 915 player-seasons partial rho(L, DeltaPPP|opp)=-0.087; MDE rho~0.23
failure_evidence: S3 rho=-0.040; MDE~0.23; 986-pool stated null

title: Season-ending spells and pre-window length robustness
hypothesis: The pre-absence ranking is produced by season-ending shutdowns or short pre windows.
design: Drop 85 season-ending spells; require n_pre>=30.
failure_evidence: ranking remains; excluding season-ending raises it to +0.549

title: Opponent scouting P1: SI does not improve play-type mix forecast
hypothesis: Adding SI relationships beats a learned conventional mix forecast (LL(F2)-LL(F3)>0) with 10% gap closure.
design: 148 spells; evaluation on spell games 6+ (2,909 team-games, 260,630 possessions); Holm family; plan fixed before execution.
failure_evidence: gap closure 0.08% vs 10% threshold; CI includes 0
notes: Mechanical removal F1 vs F0 +0.00009 p=0.80; learned retention F2 vs F0 +0.00057 p=0.002; F3b worse than F2L by -0.0053 p=0.0001.

title: Opponent scouting P2: SI leave-one-out does not forecast relationship structure
hypothesis: G1 (leave-one-out) is closer to the evaluation fingerprint than G0 (no change).
design: Same 148 evaluation sets; dist(G0)-dist(G1); Holm family.
primary_result: mean dist G0=0.145, G1=0.141, noise floor=0.085; dist(G0)-dist(G1)=+0.0032 CI[-0.0050,+0.0106] p=0.44 Holm 0.87; G1 beats G0 in 49% of spells
failure_evidence: G1 beats G0 in 49%; CI includes 0
notes: Ayton/Embiid cases show G1 help that does not generalize.

title: Opponent scouting P3: incremental R2 of L_pre for displacement magnitude
hypothesis: Adding L_pre to conventional features raises held-out R2 of displacement (bootstrap CI excluding 0 and perm passing Holm).
design: LOFO R2_oos; co-primary Y2 staleness; Holm family; pass requires bootstrap CI exclude 0.
failure_evidence: perm p=0.010 (Holm 0.030) but franchise bootstrap CI includes 0, so pre-registered pass rule fails
notes: Borderline magnitude signal, consistent with the paper's ranking claim but not established as scouting value.

title: Opponent scouting S1: high-L absences make labeled play types more predictable
hypothesis: High L_pre absences increase offensive predictability (partial Spearman of L_pre with spell-minus-pre log-loss).
design: Leave-one-game-out log-loss; label-free shot-zone and initiator checks; high-confidence labels.
primary_result: all labels rho=-0.187 CI[-0.344,-0.041] p=0.024; confidence>=0.75 rho=-0.070 p=0.43; shot zones +0.062 p=0.46; initiator identity +0.131 p=0.12
failure_evidence: label-free measures opposite sign; effect disappears in high-confidence labels; 2024-25 inferrer-share shift -42 pp
notes: Apparent predictability gain is carried by labeling, not shot zones or initiator identity.

title: Opponent scouting S2: value of early post-absence film
hypothesis: Early spell games improve mix/initiator forecasts more when L_pre is high, and an F3 prior beats F2.
design: Update after spell games 1-5; play-type and initiator (T3) log-loss gains; partial rho with L_pre.
primary_result: play types: +0.0003 after 1 game, +0.0023 after 5; F3 never beats F2 (diffs ~0.00002, p>=0.14); initiators: +0.134/+0.201/+0.233/+0.269/+0.309 after 1-5 games; partial rho with L -0.02 to -0.11
failure_evidence: early film helps initiators a lot but the gain does not rise with L_pre; F3 never beats F2
notes: Who initiates goes stale immediately; what gets run does not.

title: Opponent scouting S4: defensive attention tracks new usage, not L_pre
hypothesis: Defenses anticipate high-L absences in matchup time beyond the new usage pattern.
design: Within-team rho of change in initiation share vs attention share; games 1-5 vs 6+; moderation by L_pre.
primary_result: mean within-team rho=+0.92 [+0.91,+0.93]; early vs later attention rho=+0.54 [+0.49,+0.58]; L_pre moderation -0.169 p=0.044 (alignment) and -0.059 p=0.45 (convergence)
failure_evidence: attention almost perfectly tracks usage (rho 0.92); L_pre moderation weak; not evidence of exploitation
notes: Exploratory; Spearman(alignment, DeltaPPP)=-0.17.

title: Feasibility check: initiation share vs L_pre as predictors of D_real
hypothesis: L_pre predicts D_real after controlling initiation share; initiation share does not after controlling L_pre.
design: 148 spells; in-sample partial Spearman; franchise bootstrap/perm. Not held-out (P3 is).
primary_result: Spearman(init_share, D_real)=+0.029 CI[-0.108,+0.178] p=0.73; partial(L_pre, D_real | init_share, n_spell, n_pre)=+0.369 CI[+0.209,+0.494] p=0.0005; partial(init_share | L_pre,...)=-0.116 p=0.19; Spearman(init_share, L_pre)=+0.332
failure_evidence: L_pre partial +0.369; init_share raw +0.029
notes: In-sample reproduction of Hub Sits ranking, used to justify the scouting plan.

title: Team Adaptation gate2 restoration on a 201-spell pool
hypothesis: Cross-fitted restoration exceeds the no-absence placebo on a broader 201-spell pool (29 franchises).
design: Same gate2 cross-fit as Hub Sits; 201 rows vs paper's 148; G1 scaling and odd/even reliability also stored in gate_rows.csv.
primary_result: gate2 n=201: mean R=+0.192 vs Rp=+0.022 (diff +0.170); T=+0.157 vs Tp=+0.147 (diff +0.011); L_pre>=0.02 n=79 mean R=+0.216; gate1 n=201: R=+0.567 vs Rp=+0.416; O=+0.474 vs Op=+0.419; g1_mc median=0.0051, g1_scale median=0.0069; R split-half Spearman 0.412 (SB 0.583); O Spearman 0.609 (SB 0.757)
failure_evidence: restoration excess +0.170 on 201 spells, similar to Hub +0.173 on 148
notes: Code is a copy of Hub Sits adaptation gates run on a larger keep-set. Reliability of R (SB 0.58 on gate1 odd/even) is still below a 0.40 independent-half standard if read as gate2; this CSV is the shared-noise (gate1) construction for R. No separate writeup; inferred from CSVs.

title: Opponent three-point luck has no persistent player component
hypothesis: Opponent three-point luck is noise: split-half reliability ~0 and H1 does not predict H2.
design: 1,405 player-seasons with >=1,000 poss in each odd/even half; within-game regression on 84,641 player-games with >=10 H2 poss.
primary_result: odd/even reliability: opp 3s 0.004; opp 2s 0.463; XNET 0.585; own luck 0.477; teammate luck 0.427; PM 0.549; H1 opp3 -> H2 opp3 per 100: +0.008 (SE 0.009); H1 opp2 -> H2: +0.009 (SE 0.009)
failure_evidence: reliability 0.004; H1->H2 +0.008 SE 0.009
notes: Twos have season-level reliability 0.463 but still fail the within-game persistence check.

title: Halftime minute change weights noise like information
hypothesis: A point of opponent three-point luck moves second-half possession share less than a point of opponent two-point luck or expected net points.
design: 89,588 player-games, 4,730 games, 831 players, 2022-26 RS+PO; outcome=100*(H2 share-H1 share); FE team-game x starter and player-season; game-clustered SE.
failure_evidence: opp3-opp2=-0.002 SE 0.043; weights equal; size is ~8 seconds/SD
notes: Finding is equality of weights, not a large rotation change. Own luck is larger but not the clean noise test.

title: Halftime luck-response placebos (shuffle makes; next game; Q1)
hypothesis: The opponent-luck coefficient is an artifact of game totals or player identity, not who was on the floor when shots fell.
design: 200 shuffles of makes; next-game first-half luck predicting this game's share change (n=73,010); Q1 luck -> Q1-to-Q2 share.
primary_result: league-wide shuffle mean 0.003 (SD 0.020); within game+defense 0.029 (SD 0.017); observed 0.131; none of 200 draws reached 0.131; next-game luck -0.005 (SE 0.020) vs this-game 0.112 (SE 0.022); Q1->Q2 0.193 (SE 0.044)
failure_evidence: shuffles null; next-game luck -0.005; observed 0.131 outside all 200 draws
n_runs_note: 200 is the number of shuffle placebo draws, not independent runs

title: Halftime luck response by season, role, and score state
hypothesis: The opponent-luck coefficient is one season, one role, or blowouts.
design: Same spec on sample cuts; team-season slopes on odd vs even games (n=120).
primary_result: all 0.131 SE 0.022; seasons 0.130/0.107/0.159/0.123; starters 0.070 vs bench 0.213 (interaction -0.150 SE 0.037); close games 0.192; trail>=16 -0.037 SE 0.074; playoffs 0.327 SE 0.097; team-season odd/even r=0.09
failure_evidence: positive in every season; larger for bench; absent only when trailing by 16+
notes: Coach ranking is not possible (r=0.09). Fourth-quarter share 0.190 SE 0.036 vs third-quarter 0.075 SE 0.024.

title: Measurement study primary: in-stint evidence does not predict retained-five performance
hypothesis: Models D/E/F (actual-points, process, or all in-game evidence) beat model C on Task 2 weighted test (99% CI>0 and >=1% MSE drop).
design: Train 2022-23, val 2023-24, test 2024-25; substitution opportunities; Task 2 = same five retained, IPW; multinomial logit; 6 primary comparisons.
primary_result: NO-GO; no Task 2 99% lower bound >0; closest offense D test +0.104 millinats [-0.012, 0.219] with opposite-sign validation; Task 2 MSE changes -0.14% to +0.01% vs 1% threshold
failure_evidence: all six Task 2 comparisons fail 99% CI and 1% MSE; even 0.1% MSE would fail
notes: Feasibility profiling already showed in-game scoring is nearly uninformative. Recommendation NO-GO for an adaptive substitution policy.

title: Process measures are more reliable than points but not more predictive of later points
hypothesis: Expected shot/possession value is more reliable than actual points and better predicts later actual points.
design: Lineup-season tau and k=sigma^2/tau^2; first-half to second-half corr with later A; team-game deviations.
primary_result: lineup-season offense k: A 1,448 vs B 132 / C 126; corr later A: A 0.21, B -0.04, C 0.03 (304 lineups >=200 poss); defense A 0.06, B 0.11, C 0.13; team-game split-half A -0.11 CI[-0.14,-0.09]
failure_evidence: process 4-11x more reliable but offense corr with later points ~0; team-game actual-points component not identified
notes: Detecting 10 per 100 at 2 SE needs ~570 possessions of actual points; median lineup plays a handful per game.

title: Lineup synergy beyond player ratings is not detectable
hypothesis: A lineup layer (EB residuals of the five) improves prediction beyond ridge player ratings.
design: Weekly ridge RAPM, 770 players, penalty 2,000 set on 2022-23; EB lineup shrinkage constants on 2022-23.
primary_result: offense tau~0, k~1.4e8; defense tau=1.45 per 100, k~6,700; model B nearly identical to A; player ratings vs single-poss points r=0.03-0.04, SD of predictions 5.2 per 100
failure_evidence: offense lineup tau approximately 0

title: Task 1: process in-game evidence is detectable but negligible
hypothesis: In-game evidence improves prediction of subsequent performance under the actual rotation (Task 1).
design: Same models; Task 1 = all opportunities; 99% game-clustered CI.
primary_result: offense test E +0.147 millinats [0.049, 0.252] MSE +0.01%; F +0.139 [0.005, 0.274] MSE +0.01%; validation E/F not significant (F negative); C vs M0 ~2.1 millinats and ~1.0% MSE
failure_evidence: only Task 1 offense E/F clear 99% in test; MSE +0.01%; can reflect rotation prediction not five performance
notes: Not sufficient for GO. Carryover: 10 per 100 stint residual predicts at most ~0.4 per 100 over next five.

title: Coaches retain fives that scored well even though it does not carry forward
hypothesis: Retention is associated with in-stint scoring residuals.
design: Logistic retention on C/D/E/F features without horizon; descriptive after primary models.
primary_result: propensity AUC 0.73-0.74; +0.1 PPP shrunk offensive residual raises log-odds of retention 0.070-0.077 (CIs exclude 0 all 3 seasons); +0.1 allowed residual lowers 0.044-0.066; OR ~1.11 per SD
failure_evidence: retention tracks residuals that PAP-072/075 show do not predict later points
notes: Post-primary descriptive addition. Combined with Task 2 null: coaches respond to noise.

title: Feasibility profiling: clock/stint vs adding stint points for substitution prediction
hypothesis: Adding points scored in the current stint improves held-out prediction of within-period lineup changes beyond clock and stint length.
design: Quick GBT profiling, train 2022-23+2023-24, test 2024-25, every possession as unit (not stoppages); labeled as diagnostic not study.
primary_result: AUC clock+stint 0.721; adding stint points 0.726; ~1% of actual changes have predicted p>0.5; PPP SD 1.147; median lineup-game offensive poss=4 (p90=15); ~526 poss to detect 10/100 at 2 SE
failure_evidence: AUC 0.721 vs 0.726; wrong unit (possessions not stoppages) inflates timing AUC; report appendix flags this
notes: This is the measurement study's quick check documented in feasibility_report.md (not report.md). Motivated the preregistered measurement study.

title: Shot-mix DiD after opponent-only lineup changes (Test 1)
hypothesis: An unchanged offensive five changes 3/rim/midrange shares by a practical 3 pp after an opponent-only substitution.
design: Clean 5/5 windows; 1,054 treated / 10,567 control in 2,812 games; OLS DiD with controls; CR1 game cluster; Holm across 3 shares.
failure_evidence: all CIs include 0; MDE 3.2-3.6 pp equals the 3 pp practical threshold so small effects cannot be ruled out
notes: Amendment 1 (sample sizes only) warned 10-poss windows are underpowered (37 treated). NO-GO.

title: Shot adaptation directional and dispersion tests
hypothesis: Shot mix moves toward what incoming defenders historically allow, or treated events have more dispersed share changes than controls.
design: Shrunk defender allowed-shot profiles (k=300); variance ratio with attempt-count reweighting; 1,000 game bootstrap.
primary_result: per SD profile: 5/5 three -0.42 pp [-2.57,+1.73]; rim -1.12 [-3.16,+0.92]; variance ratio 1.05 [0.95, 1.15]; 1 SD of profile change ~0.6 pp of allowed share
failure_evidence: directional CIs include 0; variance ratio 1.05; profiles barely differ after shrinkage
notes: Secondary: TO +2.1 pp q=0.03 and FT -2.0 q=0.013 are RTM from selecting on hot pre windows (36% treated are opponent timeouts vs 9% controls).

title: Own-only substitution changes shot mix (benchmark) while opponent-only does not
hypothesis: Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.
design: Same DiD estimator on own-only change class vs opponent-only.
primary_result: own-only three +3.1 pp (SE 1.2); rim -1.1 (1.1); mid -2.0 (1.1); opponent-only all within 1.4 pp of 0
failure_evidence: own-only +3.1 pp CI excludes 0; opponent-only null
notes: Design is not blind to personnel. Fake-timing and permutation placebos consistent with null opponent effect.

title: Repeat-meeting shot-mix and response repeatability (Test 4)
hypothesis: Matchup-specific shot mix or treated-minus-control response repeats from earlier to later meetings.
design: 2,610 directed pairs with >=2 meetings; residuals net of season team and opponent levels.
failure_evidence: three-share r=0.01; 5/5 response CI includes 0; 3/3 r=0.056 is isolated/uncorrected
notes: Negative rim/PPP correlations are mechanical (season means include the compared games).

title: Substitution timing after opponent changes is almost entirely the rotation clock
hypothesis: The raw +9 pp extra substitution rate after opponent changes is an opponent-personnel response of at least 5 pp under full controls.
design: 299,539 stoppages where T did not change (59,966 treated); LPM of next-stoppage change; CR1 game cluster.
primary_result: raw +8.96 pp [+8.53,+9.39]; period x minute +0.69; +stint/fouls +0.18; full +0.83 [+0.40,+1.26]; exclude timeouts +0.78; opponent timeouts only +2.16; 5-poss secondary +0.87
failure_evidence: clock alone removes 92% of the raw gap; residual +0.83 pp is 1/6 of the 5 pp GO threshold
notes: Motivated by shot study 59.7% vs 47.7% within 5 possessions. Residual is distinguishable from 0 only because n is huge.

title: Incoming offensive personnel do not track opponent incoming types
hypothesis: When T substitutes next, Delta T three-point rate tracks Delta O three-point rate at >=0.25 SD, above a clock-matched placebo.
design: 20,050 treated windows where T substitutes next; types from earlier dates only; 200 placebos pairing Delta T with other-game Delta O in the same period-minute.
primary_result: three slope 0.011 SE 0.008 std=0.011 placebo p97.5=0.014 p=0.06; rim 0.024 SE 0.008 std=0.025 placebo p=0.005; tier benchmark 0.051 std=0.052
failure_evidence: three-point slope 0.011 SD vs 0.25 threshold, inside placebo; rim 0.025 SD is 1/10 of threshold
notes: Height/position/defensive role not in the data. Tier benchmark shows the method can detect matching at 0.05 SD.
n_runs_note: 200 is the number of placebo permutations, not independent runs

title: Substitution-response repeatability is a team clock, not opponent-specific
hypothesis: Timing or personnel response repeats across season halves or across meetings with the same opponent.
design: 90 team-seasons; 2,553 pairs; post hoc within team x period-minute.
primary_result: team-season timing r=0.59 CI[0.43,0.71] n=90; pair-specific r=-0.01 [-0.05,+0.03] n=2,553; personnel slope halves r=0.00; post hoc within clock mean effect +0.8 pp then +0.4 with stint, half-to-half r=0.27-0.32
failure_evidence: only team-level timing repeats; pair r=-0.01; post hoc: average effect vanishes inside each team's clock
notes: GO required opponent-specific repeatability. Post hoc labeled as such. Overall substitution-response recommendation NO-GO.

title: Timing of teammate restoration across 5-game bins (not run)
hypothesis: Excess restoration is immediate (E1>0, trend CI includes 0) versus gradual (trend>0).
design: 123 of 148 spells with n_pre>=25; three consecutive 5-game bins; real vs time-shifted placebo; franchise bootstrap 2,000. Specified before any timing result.
failure_evidence: methods written; 01.log shows a partial loop (spells 123, progress 20/40/60 of 123) then stop; deliberately not completed
notes: User requested the study not be run. Per-spell restoration was already known to be unreliable (PAP-054).

title: NCAA men's feature additions that improved LOSO Brier
hypothesis: Added team-season features (SOS, FT rate, neutral-site ratio, rank variance, net-rating volatility, late-season slope) improve men's LOSO/OOF Brier.
design: XGBoost then meta-ensemble LOSO CV 2003-2025; keep if any Brier drop.
failure_evidence: each kept feature lowered Brier under the log's any-improvement rule
notes: Family of kept feature tests (iters 1,4,7,9,11,12). Target metric shifted from XGB CV to OOF meta during the stack.

title: NCAA men's feature additions that raised or failed to lower Brier
hypothesis: Conference strength, tourney appearances, last-5 win%, conf-tourney win%, avg margin, 3P rate, coach tenure, tempo mismatch, late mean net rating, def consistency, home-road gap, end streak, adj off eff, POM slope, FT-rate 15/2 nudge, upset-susceptibility profile, recent-era seed weights, 8/9 sharpening, seed-gap monotonicity add signal.
design: Same LOSO/OOF protocol; revert if Brier not improved.
primary_result: examples: conf strength 0.19356 vs 0.19319; last5 0.19330 vs 0.19227; coach tenure meta 0.18146 vs 0.18063; tempo mismatch 0.18205 vs 0.18063; POM slope 0.18235 vs 0.18063; 3P rate not formally logged; FT 15v2 0.17547 vs 0.17545; recent-era seed 0.17608 vs 0.17536; monotonicity 0.17642 vs 0.17535

notes: Includes iters 2,3,5,6,8,10,13-20,22,24-26,28. Ablation: 8 extra features slightly raised meta Brier 0.18250 vs 0.18240 with 12 features.

title: Injury and All-American post-processing of OOF probabilities
hypothesis: Overlaying injury underperformance and All-American bonuses on OOF meta probabilities lowers Brier.
design: No retraining; 23 injury-touched and 135 AA-touched matchups; clip [0.025,0.975].
primary_result: baseline 0.18089; injury 0.18058; AA 0.18028; both 0.17993 (combined -0.00096)
failure_evidence: combined overlay 0.17993 vs 0.18089
notes: Most of the gain is All-American (135 touches vs 23 injuries).

title: Historical seed-line calibration blend (alpha sweep)
hypothesis: Blending model probability with historical seed-matchup win rates (1985-2025) reduces Brier, especially at extremes.
design: final_prob = alpha*model + (1-alpha)*P_hist; alpha 0.1-0.9; later chalk/tossup split and 1v16/2v15 strong pull.
failure_evidence: seed blend dropped Brier by ~0.0046, the largest single gain in the log
notes: Exps 21, 23, 27, 29 kept. Differential alpha beat flat 0.5.

title: NCAA architecture: scipy blend, temperature scaling, LightGBM, era weights
hypothesis: Replacing LR meta with a convex scipy blend, then T-scaling, adding LightGBM, and era-weighting 2016+ seasons, lowers full-chain Brier.
design: LOSO OOF; keep if improved.
failure_evidence: full chain 0.17508 to 0.17454
notes: Exps 32,34,35,36. Elo weight went to 0 in the convex blend.

title: NCAA architecture failures (SWA, Platt, beta, MLP, 2nd isotonic in-sample, RF, XGB sweep)

hypothesis: An action gets less effective the more often the defense has already seen it in the game.

hypothesis: Coaches reallocate second-half minutes in response to first-half on-court shooting luck (opponent/teammate/own) as if it were performance.

hypothesis: Game-N opponent 3P luck while on court changes a player's game N+1 share and starting status.

primary_result: G_opp3 +0.0625 (0.0180), shuffle null -0.0002 sd 0.0159 p 0.000; starting +0.00041 (0.00027) perm p 0.150/0.630; controlling game-N share G_opp3 +0.0020 (0.0178); adding expected opp 3P pts +0.0284 (0.0179); bins U-shaped (<-2SD +2.6082, >2SD +3.5205).

power_info: SD G_opp3 5.97 pts; opp 3P luck split-half reliability 0.005-0.036
related: Within-game H2 playing-time response to first-half shooting luck
notes: Luck magnitude scales with game-N minutes, predictable from design. Verdict is extractor's reading; no written conclusion.

title: Within-game on/off Absorption vs Cascade (Gap = D_A - L_on)
hypothesis: When a rotation player sits, Gap = D_A - L_on is a reliable Absorption vs Cascade trait, predicted by bench-profile redundancy, and Absorption preserves PPP.
design: N=1385 rotation player-seasons (>=400 on and off possessions), 30 franchises, 2022-24 two-way possessions; odd/even split-half of D_A and Gap; Spearman of bench cosine similarity with -Gap; PPP_off - PPP_on payoff. Balanced-size follow-up N=882 (m = min(n_on, n_off)). Platoon co-substitution diagnostic.
primary_result: Gap split-half rho=+0.591 (p=5.43e-127); D_A residualized rho=+0.489; hubs L_on>=0.05 (n=543) Gap rho=+0.599. Mechanism Spearman(agg_sim, -gap_sz)=-0.205 (p=1.13e-14), hubs -0.307. PPP payoff Spearman(-gap_sz, PPP_off-PPP_on)=-0.039 (p=0.144), hubs -0.054 (p=0.209). Balanced: Spearman(Lcos, DA_bal)=+0.345, DA_bal split-half +0.573, gap_bal +0.545. corr(D_A, co_sub_tv)=+0.312 (p=1.26e-32); partial corr(D_A, L_on | co_sub_tv, min_n, u)=+0.335.
failure_evidence: Bench-redundancy mechanism has the wrong sign (Spearman(agg_sim, -gap_sz)=-0.205); PPP payoff is null (-0.039, p=0.144); D_A correlates +0.312 with platoon co-substitution.
notes: Gap reliability is high; the Absorption vs Cascade interpretation is the part that fails. Balanced-size gaps by role: PRIMARY ORGANIZER +0.0041, SHAPER -0.0661, ROLE OCCUPANT +0.0465, TERMINAL SCORER +0.0508.

Season split: 2022-23+2023-24 vs 2024-25.

title: Defensive reorganizer 28-cell signature (odd/even cosine and trade portability)
hypothesis: A defender on the floor reliably rewires the opposing offense (DA_def above a random-split null; odd/even 28-cell signature cosine and trade portability exceed decoys).
design: Eligible defenders n_on>=1000, n_off>=800; N=1067 then 1043; 2022-24. DA_def vs matched-size random-split null; odd/even split-half; year-to-year same-team vs traded; PPP-allowed payoff. Follow-up: self-cosine vs random other-team and same-team decoys; then balanced (n_on==n_off==m) signatures.
primary_result: Gate/test3: mean DA_def 0.0712 vs null 0.0874 (paired t=-11.20), i.e. below null; size-adjusted split-half rho=-0.083 (p=0.00729); unbalanced 28-cell cosine mean=+0.4556 (t=+42.17); trade portability n=175 cosine +0.2401; Spearman(DA_def_r, dPPP_allowed)=-0.050 (p=0.1). structural_diag: self cosine +0.4491 vs random-other-team +0.1280, excess +0.3211; mover self-sim +0.2432 vs decoy +0.1193, excess +0.1239, 62.3%>0, binom p=0.001. def_sig_check: BALANCED odd-even self-cosine mean=+0.0371 vs unbalanced +0.4516; share_on-matched different-team cosine unbalanced +0.4583, balanced +0.0298; balanced mover portability mean=+0.0340.
failure_evidence: Observed DA_def is below the random-split null (0.0712 vs 0.0874). The +0.45 odd/even cosine collapses to +0.0371 when n_on and n_off are balanced, and a share_on-matched different-team defender matches the unbalanced cosine (+0.4583).
notes: Initial runs treated the 28-cell cosine as a positive signal; the balanced-size check is the final version. Unequal on vs off samples were in the eligibility rule (n_on>=1000, n_off>=800).

title: 148-spell pre-absence L_pred vs realized displacement D_real
hypothesis: Pre-absence Structural Influence L_pred_pre predicts balanced realized displacement D_real in the 148 registered absence spells, including after size and usage controls and in non-season-ending windows.
design: 148 spells, 28 franchises, 65 team-seasons; m=min(n_spell, floor(n_pre/2)); D_real = mean 1-cos(A(m pre), A(m spell)); size-partial Spearman with franchise perm p and cluster bootstrap. Reviewer splits: usage tercile, drop season-ending, pre window >=30/40 games, pre vs full-season L.
primary_result: N=148; above own p95 65/148 (43.9%), binom p=3.2e-44; mean excess +0.0748. raw Spearman(L_pred_pre, D_real)=+0.357 perm p=0.0005 CI [+0.209, +0.470]; size-partial +0.353 p=0.0005 CI [+0.209, +0.465]; Spearman(L_pred_pre, excess)=+0.299. L_pred_pre>=0.10: 8/8 above p95, mean excess +0.2115. Look-ahead L_season vs D_real +0.288 vs pre +0.357; Spearman(pre, season)=+0.608. R1 paired difference pre-season +0.069 [-0.122, +0.250]. R4 also controlling usage +0.356 [+0.214, +0.468] perm p=0.0005; top usage tercile n=50 +0.521 [+0.288, +0.700]. R5 excluding season-ending n=63 +0.549 [+0.373, +0.680]. R7 pre>=30 n=98 +0.317; pre>=40 n=56 +0.350.
failure_evidence: size-partial rho=+0.353, perm p=0.0005, CI [+0.209, +0.465]; survives usage control and dropping season-ending spells.
notes: stage2_outcomes.log died mid-cases on a UnicodeEncodeError; pool stats were complete and were reused by stage2_cases/cases2. R1 pre vs season difference CI includes 0. See TMP-028 for the mechanical-floor challenge to interpreting D_real as extra reorganization.

title: Mechanical floor and drift placebo of absence displacement
hypothesis: L_pred_pre predicts displacement beyond the mechanical effect of deleting the player row (R2) and beyond pre-window drift with the player still present (R3).
design: 148 spells; mechanical floor = distance from m pre games to m other pre games with the player row removed (20 reps); drift placebo = first half vs second half of the pre window, player present. Size-partial Spearman of L_pre with floor, with D_real minus floor, and with drift; franchise perm.
primary_result: mean D_real 0.152, mechanical floor 0.102, drift 0.101; 78% of spells have D_real above floor. High-load: D_real 0.285, floor 0.241, excess +0.044; low-load: D_real 0.145, floor 0.094, excess +0.051. size-partial rho(L_pre, mechanical floor)=+0.432 [+0.336, +0.528] perm p=0.0005; rho(L_pre, D_real minus floor)=+0.082 [-0.104, +0.251] perm p=0.3358; rho(L_pre, drift)=+0.094 [-0.043, +0.218] perm p=0.3033; rho(L_pre, D_real) controlling drift=+0.345 [+0.182, +0.480] perm p=0.0005.
failure_evidence: rho(L_pre, D_real minus mechanical floor)=+0.082, perm p=0.3358, CI includes 0; L_pre tracks the floor itself (+0.432). Excess above floor is similar for high-load (+0.044) and low-load (+0.051).
power_info: n=148; 20 replicates; CI on excess association [-0.104, +0.251]
notes: Deleting a high-L row necessarily moves the fingerprint; that was computable from the estimator. Drift placebo does not explain the raw L-D association, but the floor does.

title: Paper 1 season-level L vs March-April 2025 labeling switch
hypothesis: The March-April 2025 play-type labeling switch changes season-level Structural Influence L and role classes beyond the effect of merely dropping post-March games (2023-24 placebo).
design: Label-source shares by month; then L from all regular-season games vs games before March 1 for 2023-24 (clean) and 2024-25 (switch). First run used case_common std_A; definitive run used published pull_edges / build_B_labeled_by_id / loo_loads with 500 nulls. Monte Carlo baseline: this-run all-games L vs published Lcos.
primary_result: Label shares 2024-25: Oct inferrer 0.827 / Apr inferrer 0.016 untagged 0.798; Mar inferrer 0.499. Definitive 500-null run: 2023-24 n=414, rho(this run, published)=0.755, rho(all games, before March 1)=0.667 (L>=0.03 n=61: 0.772), high-load>=0.10: 16 full / 15 trunc / 16 published. 2024-25 n=439, rho(this run, published)=0.719, rho(all, trunc)=0.690 (L>=0.03 n=72: 0.819), high-load: 19 / 22 / 21. First run (different estimator): 2023-24 Spearman(full,trunc)=0.465 median |diff|=0.0070, 19 high-load flips; 2024-25 0.531 / 0.0084 / 20 flips; role-class print crashed (TypeError).
